scores.why: Yardstick. It has the lit-tube soul (halo on the mark, mind and Send, the glowing monitors), but it is the bright, contrasty, nearly all-green page the owner asked to calm. There is no grounded colour, no line art and no structure beyond cards.

The biggest owner-shaped step this round. One real terminal on every page, in a thin graphite case, holds the question typed on the glass ('What's on your mind?' with a cursor), warms up from a bright line, and ends in a lit 'Ready' foot. A numbered Contents plate on a rail of rings sits beside a calm slate desk of one-line rows with rails and a NOW lamp. The light sits where the machine is and grounded colour everywhere else, and it changes every page (Home, Status, Plans, To do, Chat), not a corner.

The leader, refined the way the owner wants. The tube now draws the coming weeks, and lit rails run from now through Coming up, To do and Status's Who answers. A tuning scale sits under the bar, and big tabular head figures ('4 PLANS', '12 IDEAS') count as real typesetting gains. Only the squeezed portrait radar on Ideas and the barcode-small trace hold it back.

Still the most complete carrier of the Signal Box line language the owner loves: the Coming up track with a lit now, the To do timetable with lamps, Chat hung from Vera's mark, the Status rails and the dot under the current page. Its lamps and tubes are relit. It loses ground on rounded plates and cards, an icon-only right bar, and a weaker listing structure than the Evening Listing line.

Long Persistence plus a phosphor panel meter on the Status tube, drawn in the tube's light with a bright needle and halo. Printed registers and gauges sit beside it in bone on graphite. That is exactly 'light where it's live, print elsewhere' and a genuine CRT instrument. Home and the other pages change only by a modest engraved rule.

Calm, grounded and well typeset: a slate listing with a head column, steel reverse video, denim links and the tube's light on a short list. It is the right system, but its line art is limited to Coming up, and the phosphor soul lives mostly in the greeting.

Tubes that draw the family's own data (the weeks on Next up, due dates on To do, spend on Status) are strong CRT DNA doing a job, and the graphite legend tables with column heads are grounded and legible. It has little line art, and the Home tables read a bit generic.

It brings back the original's page glow as a scanlined green afterglow over each page head, and Next up becomes a terminal with a prompt. That is in the owner's direction, but it is subtle at page scale, reads as a haze in the corner, and leaves blank lit glass between the date and the prompt. Otherwise it is its parent.

A good crossover. The Status annunciator of lit tiles is a convincing lit-panel CRT moment, and it adds a sentence-case bar with lamps, a readout strip, flight-plan arcs that carry order, and amber-edged late cards. It is let down by a 2100px Home, console costume labels ('CONSOLE 09 | SYSTEMS') and chunky bays.

Signal Legend Relit with a thoughtful width-axis type system (condensed titles, normal text, wide nameplate caps), which the owner's love of typesetting rewards. The colour and structure are unchanged from its parent, and the slashed zeros on the glass blur ('$0.00').

The most CRT soul after Desk Terminal. The question is typed on a big green tube, each page has its own green screen summarising it, the power-on starts from a line, and the rest is grounded graphite with measured heather, cornflower and sea caps. It loses on empty cells (Memory, Wishes), text wrapping in narrow cells, tracked-caps buttons, brass warmth and heavy boxed item cards.

Beautiful rails with heads set into them, a Coming up track with a lit now, and steel reverse video. The owner liked Signal Legend. The glow on the bubble edges spreads the light to things that are not live, and today's newer entrants carry the same ideas further.

Teletext is a true period CRT, and its lower-chroma CGA-like section colours, page numbers and mosaic drawings are the kind of 'computer colour scheme' the owner floated. But the double-height VT323 heads in pink, amber, lemon and lilac at 40px make it the loudest, most colourful page here, the opposite of 'less bright, less contrasty', and 46 of 56 Home targets are small.

The instrument language is strong (readout strip, flight-plan arcs, T-minus setup, crew board), but it has tracked mono caps for nav and links and a mostly grey page. Its crossover child, Slate Flight Console, now does it better.

Lovely and wondrous: a star-chart dome with fine meridians and Vera at the zenith. But it is a planetarium, not a green-screen terminal, with serif type, a teal night ground, maroon family bubbles and a starfield. The plan stars carry no labels, so the chart is decoration more than structure.

The question on the glass and a numbered Contents are real CRT soul. The brown plastic case, pastel filled tiles, VT323 band heads and a nav moved to foot keys are off-motif for the owner (brown was his least favourite).

A title with its figure in the section colour is a neat typographic device, and the one-sided quote chat with the newest line set large is fresh. The plum-violet housings are the off-period purple the owner pushes back on, it is 88% green by colour share, and 53 of 59 targets are small.

The idea of the green tube glowing up through a hole torn in the page is clever. But kraft, masking tape, ransom letters and red marker are the warm, crafty, off-motif materials the owner rejected (Reading Room's browns), and the calm CRT character is gone.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the terminal-per-page system, the question typed on the glass, the warm-up from a line, the Contents plate on its ring rail and the Ready foot. Five fixes. (1) Join the typing to the glass: give the textarea a green-black glass tint and a lit prompt caret, so the question and the answer area read as one screen, with FROM, mic and Send on the deck below. (2) Shorten Home's terminal, which is about 930px: set the three ways to start as one compact row, and make the column position:sticky so it never leaves a tall empty slab. On pages with nothing live, collapse it to tube plus foot. (3) Give the case a smaller radius (about 6px) and a 1px bezel, keeping it thin and detailed rather than a rounded slab. (4) Graft Traced's lit rail from now (Coming up and To do) and its big tabular head figures onto the desk bands. (5) Remove the Settings bank duplication and keep the bar icons' section tints muted.

Three fixes to the tubes, then the rows. (1) Return the Ideas radar to a landscape tube in the listing header, or widen the head column; the 212px portrait tube wraps VT323 at 17 characters. (2) Make the Next up trace's pulses taller and label the next one on the glass, so it reads as weeks, not a barcode. (3) Let Status rows run the band's width, or split them in two columns, so 230px of empty band does not remain. For the rows: drop the long 'Thursday 1 October' column where the day tile already says it, and make the hover afterglow a steel wash with a sage edge so it never reads as a selected state.

Keep every line (the tracks, timetable, Chat thread, Status rails and the dot under here). Put words back in the bar for Memory, Family and Status, restore the amber 'was due' words, square and thin the plates, and move Ideas from cards to Evening Listing's one-line rows along a leader.

Keep the phosphor panel meter; it is the best tube instrument yet. Show the needle at a resting peg with a lit zero, and hold the power-on kick long enough to be seen. Flatten the register wheels a touch. Carry the engraved thick-then-thin rule into each band head with the section's title set in the break, so Home changes visibly too.

Keep the question on the glass, each page's own green summary screen, the graphite rack and the measured section caps. Six fixes: (1) Keep the main pages in the bar on Home too. (2) Collapse empty cells: span Memory and Family, and set Wishes at half height. (3) Stop wrapping titles in narrow cells by giving the To do cell a wider span. (4) Set buttons in sentence case, not tracked caps. (5) Keep brass to page numbers only. (6) Turn the Ideas cards into one-line rows.

Keep the page numbers, the mosaic drawings and the teletext colour idea. Limit double-height VT323 to the page title. Set section heads in condensed sans at about 1.5rem beside their mosaic icon. Put the section colour only in the dashed rule and the drawing, never in 40px text. Drop the pink. Bring the targets up to 44px.

Keep the meridian thread that falls from her screen through the Chat, and the idea of plans placed by time on a chart. Redraw the chart as a green scope on black glass (a radar or a polar plot with labelled plans), and return to sans type and the green-black ground. Family bubbles go in steel, not maroon.
Keep the Status annunciator of lit tiles and the readout strip. Drop the 'CONSOLE nn' costume labels, shorten Home by folding the flight-plan figure into Coming up's head, and thin the bays.

The one thing worth carrying: the tube seen through a window cut in the page. Translate it to a clean bevelled cut-out in slate, with the tube's light spilling onto the cut edge. Drop the kraft, tape and marker.

judges.notes: Through the owner's lens, this round's clearest advance is the terminal returning as a structural element rather than a lit corner. Desk Terminal (r12-idea-2) and Videotex Switchboard (r12-wmut-1) both type Vera's question on the green glass under a cursor and warm the tube up from a bright line. Those are the original page's own marks of a lit tube, used where the machine speaks. The rest of each page stays grounded: slate, graphite, steel and denim, with amber for 'needs a look'. That is the owner's 'bring some of that back' and 'bright green where it needs to be, grounded elsewhere' at once, and it shows on every page, not in a greeting corner. Desk Terminal wins because it also keeps what the tournament gained: one-line rows with tabular facts, a Contents rail of numbered rings, a Coming up rail from a NOW lamp, and a Chat track ending in a ring. That is the line language the owner calls high style, carried through Status, Plans and To do as a system. Evening Listing, Traced is the best refinement of the leader: lit rails from now, a tube that draws data, head figures, and a tuning scale. Track Diagram Relit remains the fullest carrier of the Signal Box lines. The ideal next breed is Desk Terminal's terminal (question on glass, Contents plate, Ready foot), Traced's lit rails and head figures on the desk, Track Diagram's Chat thread and dot under here, and Metered's phosphor panel meter as Status's tube. Avoid: warm materials (brass in quantity, kraft, brown cases, maroon bubbles), violet or plum housings, VT323 at display size off the glass, empty lit glass, and pastel filled headlines. The afterglow haze in r12-mut-4 is the right instinct but too faint to change the page; light pays when it sits on something live, not as a wash.

scores.why: The source of the soul: every lit thing has its full halo, the greeting glows from below, the tubes bloom and the cursor blinks. But the glow is not scarce. Green runs through every icon, link and button, so the page glares rather than being lit where attention belongs.

The most complete return of the tube on this panel. Every page has one real terminal, and its glass draws that page's own data. The question is typed on the glass under a block cursor, To do shows ASCII late bars with amber on the phosphor, Status shows the spend, Plans a trace and Ideas the radar. It warms up from a bright line, the latched key has a lit LED, and the desk beside it stays matte. Light is where attention belongs on Home, To do, Status and Plans alike.

The light goes to work. Next up's spare glass becomes a four-week pulse trace, and the rails are lit from a breathing NOW lamp on Coming up and To do (between the late and the upcoming tasks). Status's Who answers chain glows from lamp to lamp. Glow reaches below the fold without spreading. The trace reads like a small barcode at 1x, and the Ideas radar is squeezed into a narrow portrait tube.

The phosphor needle meter on Status is the most period-true lit graphic of the round: a green scale with hatched overrun, a hot needle core and a halo. Every page keeps a tube that draws the family's data. Held back because the needle rests at zero in the stills, the Next up sweep beam still crosses the words, and Home barely differs from its parent.

You type on the glass: the question and a block-cursor prompt sit on the Home tube, and Chat's box is a lit '> Message Vera' prompt. Every page gets its own summary screen (DUE NEXT on To do, the month on Plans, 9 parts on Settings), and the tubes warm up from a line. The graphite rack with brass numbers is heavy, and some screens only repeat their cells.

The tube draws the family's own weeks, due dates, spend and places, with full bloom, scanlines and sweep, and the legend tables stay matte. The sweep beam still crosses the text on Next up, and the resting pulses are low.

Now lamps are white-hot points in a breathing halo, and the track from each lamp to the next stop is lit, on Coming up, To do's timetable and Status. That is still the best 'lit where live' line. This round's terminals and meters now do more with the light than brightening lamps.

Real terminal behaviour: a command path in the bar ending in a blinking cursor, an LED on the current key, a row of glowing lamps on Status, and Next up flashing in inverse as it arrives, with the tubes at full bloom. The plum-graphite housing and big section-coloured figures lean toward a trading floor, and Chat as a flat transcript loses her lit marks.

It brings back the original's top haze, scanlines under the bar and the greeting's pool, and Next up gets a prompt on its last row. But on Chat, Ideas, Status, Plans and To do the afterglow is a faint haze at the top left that barely registers. That is a wash in the corner, not new light on the content.

The tubes are at full strength, the greeting pool and scanlines are back, Status lamps glow as dots and Chat ends in a lit ring. It is calm and grounded, but below the greeting the page is matte listing, with little that glows because it is live.

The most CRT-hearted first screen here: the question on the glass under a cursor, a big radar, a warm-up from a line and an LED on the current key. The brown plastic case and VT323 band heads turn it toward a kiosk costume.

The Status annunciator is the round's best lamp panel: working systems are lit green glass tiles with a lamp bar, and those that are off stay dark. The big Home radar blooms, and the bar's keys carry lamp dots. The flight-plan figure and T-minus costume are matte drawings rather than light, and they fill Home before the family's rows do.

Teletext on a warm TV: double-height pixel headlines, 'mind' glowing, an afterglow that visibly fades on rows, and a warm-up on Next up. It is a true CRT-era voice. But the mosaic drawings and the VT323 used for dates, labels and heads are flat, so the terminal voice is everywhere rather than scarce, and the apostrophe stands as a tall tick.

The halo is on mind, Send and the lamps, the monitors bloom, and a now lamp opens the Coming up track. The glowing bubble edges in Chat spread light to things that are not live, and nothing new is lit.
Its parent's light, unchanged. The slashed zero on the glass is a nice terminal touch, but in full bloom it blurs into a blob at the Next up size, and the wide capital labels add no light.
True tube behaviour (a warm-up, green afterglow on cards, an annunciator of lamps), but the grey plotting grids and tracked mono-caps nav make it an admin cockpit more than a lit tube.

Lit and a little wondrous: Vera glows at the zenith, the next plan pings green on the meridian, and the radar survives on Ideas. But the dome's teal-green bloom washes the whole of Home, starlight and a parchment serif turn it into a planetarium, and Next up shrinks to a letterbox strip that is no longer a 4:3 monitor.

The torn holes where the green tube glows up through the card are the most literal 'light through the page', and they bloom hard. But tape, cut-out letters, red marker and grain replace the Phosphor personality with a punk zine, and the chunky pixel face on the glass is no longer the P1 green-screen type.

fixes.suggestion: Keep one terminal per page, the warm-up from a bright line, the question on the glass and the ASCII late bars; this is the standard's light rule made visible. (1) Put the typed words on the glass too: make the ask field the tube's last row, as Switchboard does, so the family's words glow as they type. (2) Chat has no tube. Give its terminal her screen at full bloom, or a small scope of today's thread, not only a portrait and a Ready foot. (3) The row afterglow is invisible in every capture. Add a 10-14% steel wash with a 2px sage edge that fades over 1.2s. (4) On pages with nothing live (form, Wishes, Family), collapse the terminal to its foot, so no graphite slab sits over empty desk. Keep Home's terminal inside the first viewport.

Keep the lit rails from NOW and the Status chain; they are the best way yet to carry light below the fold. Make the Next up trace taller, with the next pulse labelled on the glass, so it reads as a scope, not a barcode. Put the Ideas radar back in a 4:3 tube (under the filters at full width, or beside the list); a narrow portrait tube wraps its words at 17 characters. Make the row afterglow visible (a steel wash with a sage edge fading over 1.2s).

Keep the phosphor needle meter; it is the round's best lit graphic. Show a ghost of the day's peak, or yesterday's reading, so the dial reads as a measurement even at $0.00. Clip Next up's sweep beam to the trace strip under the words so it never crosses text. Flatten the printed registers (no number wheels), so light versus print stays the rule. Let Home carry one new lit element, for example the meter's small twin in the setup or spend row, since Home now differs only by the rule.

Keep typing on the glass and the lit '>' prompt in Chat, and one summary screen per page. Size the Home tube to its content: about 100px of empty glass sits between the radar and the question. Let each screen say something its cells do not (late count, next due, today's spend) rather than repeating them. Collapse empty cells (Memory, Wishes) so the rack does not read as a wall of boxes. Quiet the brass page numbers a step, so the only warm light is the amber 'needs a look'.

The teletext page is a genuine CRT voice worth keeping: page numbers, the double-height headline, mosaic drawings and a working afterglow. Keep VT323 to the headline, page numbers and tubes, and set dates, labels and the [IN 2 DAYS] asides back in Plex Mono, so the terminal voice is scarce again. Give the double-height headline's key word the E1 halo and leave the rest of it matte. Fix the stretched apostrophe.

Keep the command path with its blinking cursor, the LED on the current key, the lamp row on Status and the inverse flash on arrival; all four are phosphor behaviours the standard could adopt. Give Chat back her lit marks (her screen glyphs at the bubble, or a lit speaker column). Move the plum surfaces toward neutral graphite so the housing does not compete with the tube.

The afterglow is too faint to register on inner pages. Either let it land on something (the steel title tile catching a visible green rim, or scanlines across the title's lit tile only) or drop it and spend the effort on lit data, as Traced does. Keep the prompt on Next up's last row, but fill or trim the 40px of blank glass above it.

Keep the meridian thread in Chat and the idea of plans as stars rising over her screen, but label the stars and contain the bloom to Vera's screen and the one pinging next star, so the dome is not a green wash over Home. Restore a 4:3 chinned tube for Next up, and replace the parchment serif with the page's sans.

The torn hole with the tube glowing through it is a striking scarcity device: one per page, only where the machine is live. Put VT323 back on the glass (the chunky pixel face loses the P1 look), and drop the tape, cut-out letters and grain from every scrap, so the light, not the craft, is the personality.

judges.notes: Through the soul lens, the round's clear advance is light that works on every page, not light added to the greeting. Desk Terminal, Traced, Metered and Switchboard each give Home, To do, Status and Plans their own lit instrument drawing that page's data: ASCII late bars, pulse traces, a needle meter, per-page summary screens, and the question typed on the glass. That is both the owner's 'bring back the phosphor' and 'reflect more of the page content'. Pure haze returns (Afterglow's scanlined wash under the bar) barely register at page scale and read as a wash in the corner. The wild entrants that swap the CRT for another metaphor (zine, planetarium) keep glowing tubes but lose the personality. Ceefax and Single Quote keep a CRT-era voice, but VT323 spread across the page (Ceefax) makes the terminal voice common rather than scarce. Every entrant still has an invisible row afterglow in the captures, the fourth round running. The breed my lens wants: Desk Terminal's one lit terminal per page with its warm-up; Switchboard's typing on the glass and its lit Chat prompt; Metered's needle; Traced's lit rails from NOW below the fold. Everything else stays matte slate. Green share on the leaders (55-68%) and a non-green neon share under 7% show that this light need not cost the grounded colour.

scores.why: Yardstick. It has the original tube's soul (bloom, halo, lit words), but the glow and the green are spread evenly across the whole page, with no second material and no typographic voice. That is why the family said it looks like the Matrix.

The clearest new identity of the round, and it holds as a system on every page: one cased, lit terminal stands at the left and the matte desk beside it holds only the family's rows. The question is typed on the glass with a cursor, To do's tube draws Late, This week and Later as phosphor bars, Status's tube holds the spend, and the status foot gives the machine a presence on every page. Numbered band rings and a Contents plate with leaders are good typesetting. The light is back exactly where the machine is.

The most wondrous page here, and the one a family would call lovely. Vera sits at the zenith of a charted dome and the plans rise as stars on 1w/2w/4w rings. Atlas serif names, small caps with Greek letters (α β γ δ) as section numerals, red-lamp mono for coordinates only, and maroon bubbles for the family's own words make a fresh, considered mood. It loses points because the dome lives only on Home, the pill buttons soften the machine's controls, and the other pages are mostly a change of type and teal.

A confident editorial device that works on every page: a condensed title followed by its figure in the section's colour ('Ideas 12', 'Things to do 4', 'Settings 1'), a command path in the bar ('> STATUS▌'), and a lamp row with big counts on Status. The plum-graphite housing is a subtle, fresh warmth. It loses points for the busy two-row numbered bar with its ALT legend, the odd near-title size given to the first To do item and to Chat's last line, and tape type that is too small.

A genuinely new structure. Home is the service's sommaire, a switchboard of page cells, each with its number, a leader and a count, plus pixel pictograms. The big tube has the question typed on the glass, and every page opens the same rack with its own green screen. It is coherent and memorable. It loses points for heavy boxing (caps, borders and rules on every cell) and for cells that stretch half-empty (Memory, the Status plate), which read as a widget dashboard.

Adds real character to Long Persistence. A phosphor moving-coil needle on the spend tube, an odometer register and edgewise meters in bone ink turn Status into an instrument panel while the green stays on the one live dial. Everywhere else the change from the parent is only the engraved rule, and the needle resting at zero reads as dead in stills.

The light is the data: the Next up scope draws the weeks and To do's scope draws due dates, set against print-like graphite legend tables with real column heads. Refined and grounded, though Home below the fold is a well-made but conventional table page.

Evening Listing with its light put to work. Rails are lit from the now lamp, large head-column figures ('4 PLANS', '12 IDEAS') make a good typographic step, and Next up has a trace. The trace reads as a barcode at 1x, and the portrait radar squeezed into the Ideas head column is cramped. It is a tasteful refinement more than a new voice.

A calm, well-typeset programme listing: condensed heads, a head column that says how things stand, steel reverse video, and the tube relit on the greeting. It is a strong, coherent system, but next to this round's entrants it reads as a polished dark dashboard rather than a memorable identity.

Brings the original tube's light back as a scanlined afterglow falling from the bar, and Next up becomes a proper terminal. At page scale, though, the afterglow reads as a soft green haze in each page's top-left corner, the 'wash in the corner' the owner named, over a page otherwise identical to its parent.

Flight Console rebuilt in slate. The Status annunciator of lit green tiles is striking, and the radar-first Home with its readout strip, flight-plan arcs and banded rows has real period flavour. The console costume ('CONSOLE 03 · TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY', T-minus) is charming but opaque, and the page is long and busy.

The mimic-line idea is distinctive: a track with lamps through Coming up, the To do due column and the chat thread. The lit stretch from now is a nice rule. Its rounded cards and panels feel softer and more generic than the idea deserves.

A pleasing typographic change: narrow Archivo titles give a timetable feel, and there are slashed zeros. But it is the parent page with new type, so it nearly fails the 'looks identical' test, and the wide caps labels get louder without gaining meaning.

A bold, cheerful teletext identity with a real illustration system: mosaic drawings at every head, page numbers in the bar and tinted head bands. It is memorable, and the kids would love it. But VT323 at double height everywhere (a huge headline, 25px dates, a tall apostrophe) and bright section-coloured heads make it loud and costume-like rather than grounded.

A period instrument language (readout strip, flight-plan arcs, annunciator) with real atmosphere. Tracked mono caps on the nav and the controls, and a costume that repeats information, keep it from reading as a considered standard.
A tidy system of rails with heads set into them and steel reverse video, with the phosphor relit. It reads closest to today's page with steel added, and in this company it is timid.

The most faithful Minitel mood, with the question on the glass and a numbered Contents. The brown plastic case, VT323 band heads, pastel tiles and a foot key row make it heavy and more theme-park than standard.

The boldest and most handmade entry: torn black card, the tube glowing up through holes torn in the page, and red marker rings for 'here'. It is crafted with wit, but ransom-note titles at one size, masking tape on every scrap and grain everywhere tip into gimmick, and it no longer reads as the Phosphor Interface.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the rule (a lit, cased terminal where the machine speaks and a matte, square desk for the family's rows), the typed question with its cursor, the To do bar tube, the Contents plate and the status foot. Fixes: (1) build the ask field into the terminal's own deck (same graphite body, a keyboard ledge under the glass) so that the question on the glass and the field below it read as one instrument, not a tube plus a loose form; (2) on Chat, the left terminal should show her glyph screen with the kids' conversations as its Contents plate, and on thin pages (Wishes, Family, the new-idea form) collapse it to a slim sticky terminal so no empty column hangs under a small box; (3) make the terminal sticky, so its foot never falls below the fold on a long Home; (4) swap VT323's curly apostrophe for a straight one on the glass.

Keep the zenith/meridian composition, the plans as stars, the atlas serif with small-caps heads and Greek section numerals, red lamp for coordinates only, and maroon for the family's own words. Fixes: (1) make the dome a system rather than Home's backdrop: give each page head a quiet arc of the chart that plots its own data (Plans on the week rings, To do's due dates on the hour ring, Status's live lamps as stars); (2) keep the ground nearer black and let the teal glow only inside the dome; (3) square the Send pill and the chips to the page's radius so the machine's controls stay Phosphor keys; (4) label the next plan's star on the glass; (5) bring the 40 small targets up to 44px.

Keep the title-plus-figure device in the section colour, the command path with its cursor in the bar, the lamp row and counts on Status, and the plum-graphite housing. Fixes: (1) fold the two-row numbered bar into one row, showing the number keys and the ALT legend only on focus; (2) set the 'quoted' To do item and Chat's latest line one step below the title, not near title size, and quote the next-due or unanswered item rather than whatever is first; (3) raise the tape type to 15px.

Keep the sommaire Home (cells with page number, leader and count), the question typed on the big tube, the pixel pictograms and the brass page numbers. Fixes: (1) cut the rule weight by keeping the coloured top cap on Home's page cells only and dropping borders to one hairline; (2) let cells size to their content (span rows, or two-up where the content is small) so Memory, the Status plate and the Plans column never stand half-empty; (3) merge the plate and the tube in column 1 on inner pages so the rack opens with one object, not three stacked boxes.

Keep the phosphor needle on the spend tube and the printed registers. In stills, show the ghost trail of the day's peak and give a resting needle a faint live flicker so it reads as a reading, not a dead dial. Carry one small printed meter to Home's head column so the idea reaches the first page.

Keep the mosaic drawings (they are a real pictogram system), the page numbers and the service voice. Set heads in condensed sans at about 1.5rem, with the section colour only in the drawing and the dashed rule. Keep VT323 for the glass, page numbers and dates on a tube. Return the tinted head bands to neutral slate.

Two ideas are worth breeding out of the zine: the tube glowing up through a torn hole in the page (light behind the surface), and a hand-drawn marker ring for 'here'. Set titles in real type, with one cut-out letter at most, keep one piece of tape per page, and lighten the grain.

Its afterglow reads as a corner wash. Attach the light to the lit tile only (a tight layered halo that comes up in 0.12s and fades over 1.2s) or run it as a faint full-width scanline band under the bar, and let the new Next up terminal carry the change.

judges.notes: Through the style lens the round moved forward: four entrants (Desk Terminal, Zenith Desk, Single Quote, Videotex Switchboard) change the whole page with a clear, memorable idea while keeping grounded colour and putting the phosphor light back where the machine speaks. None is only a wash in the corner. Desk Terminal wins because its idea is a rule that holds on every page (the machine states in a lit terminal, the desk holds the family's rows), and it brings back the original tube's soul (the question typed on glass with a cursor, bloom and scanlines, data drawn in light) without glare. Zenith Desk has the most lyrical mood and the best typographic detail (Greek section numerals, atlas small caps, a red lamp kept for coordinates). It needs the dome made into a system that reaches beyond Home. Single Quote shows that a single typographic device, a title with its figure in the section colour, can carry identity across the whole app. Worth trying next: Desk Terminal's terminal-and-desk rule with Single Quote's title-plus-figure heads and command path, and Zenith's Greek or small-caps section numbering as the band marks. The refinements of the Evening Listing and Long Persistence families are well made but now read as the safe centre. The afterglow mutant confirms that ambient green haze reads as a wash; light needs an object to sit on. Teletext and zine prove that loud costume (VT323 everywhere, tape everywhere) costs taste even when the drawing and craft are good; their best parts (mosaic pictograms, light through a torn hole) are worth keeping as details. Today's page is the yardstick at 4.4; the best is 8.0.

scores.why: Consistent but not a system: rounded glowing cards on every surface, no written type scale, pill-bubbles, glow spread evenly so nothing is ranked. It is today's yardstick.

The first entrant that is a page template, not a palette. On every page the machine column holds the tube, the latched-key deck, a numbered 'On this page' plate and a status foot. The matte, square desk holds the family's one-line rows, with leaders, column heads and ringed band numbers. 'Lit versus matte' becomes layout, and the tube's warm-up from a bright line brings the original's light back exactly where attention belongs. Held back by a cramped Home composer (chips wrap in the ~400px column), an inner scrollbar in the Ideas terminal, an almost empty terminal on the form page, and the Settings pages listed twice.

The listing system at its most complete. Every head column states a figure (4 PLANS, 4 OPEN / 2 late link, 12 IDEAS), every list carries column heads, a NOW marker slots into To do between late and future, the kind filter is a single control, and the tube draws a four-week trace. It holds on Home, Ideas, To do, Status and Plans alike. The losses: Coming up says the date twice, Status's 44rem measure leaves a dead band on the right, the amber row afterglow on setup reads as selected, and the portrait radar in the Ideas head column is thin.

Still a sound standard: bands with a head column, one-line rows to tabular facts, steel reverse video for 'here', denim links, and 0 small targets. Its two children now each do something it doesn't: one makes every head column a figure, the other adds the tube's afterglow.

The parent kept whole, plus one rule that would hold on any page: the tube's afterglow falls from the bar onto each page's lit tile and title. The owner's 'bring the light back' is answered without spreading glare. At page scale it is a faint haze, though, and Next up's roughly 40px of blank glass breaks the 'no lit glass that is empty' rule.

Adds a real instrument vocabulary with clear jobs: what is live (today's spend) is a phosphor needle dial, and what is past is printed registers, meters and split bars. An engraved lead-and-hairline rule divides every page's parts. Status now reads at a glance. Everywhere else it is the parent, whose sweep beam still crosses Next up's text and whose Status tables wrap in narrow thirds. The register's number wheels lean skeuomorphic.

True column heads and tubes that draw the family's own data are strong system traits. It is held back by the sweep beam crossing text, Status's three narrow tables wrapping every cell, and a Home split into two equal columns that loses the listing's single measure.

Lines carry order (the Coming up track, To do's timetable margin, Chat hung from her mark), which is a good rule. But the Ideas cards and Status's boxed rows fall back to generic cards, and the lit stretch of track barely shows in stills.

A real grid system. Every page is the same four-column rack of equal cells, each headed by one contents line (lamp, page number, name, leader, count), and the prompt is typed on the glass: the best 'map of the service' Home yet. It loses points for tracked caps on controls (ADD AN IDEA, SEND, TELL VERA SOMETHING), cells stretched empty to their row (Memory, the Wishes kids), Ideas and To do set as cards instead of rows, and no page keys on Home itself.

A clean typographic rule: one variable face whose width axis carries the rank (narrow for big titles, normal for what is read, wide for tiny labels), plus slashed zeros. It is worth grafting. It rides on Signal Legend's weaker frame, though (olive setup tray, rail legends), and the wide caps date now rivals her name.

Flight Console made usable: sentence-case nav, a readout strip of figures, slate banding and steel 'here'. Status as a grid of lamp plates is clear, but the lit plates fill surfaces with green. The CONSOLE 09 costume, a Home about 2100px long, Ideas as cards and To do cards set 3-up keep it from reading as one system with the listing pages.

The 'quote one thing large, tape the rest' hierarchy is a genuine new rule that could hold on every page. The quoted figures in section colour, the compact 1300px Home and Chat's last line set large all work. Against it: a plum-graphite tint (hue 304) over every surface, tracked mono caps legends everywhere (even inline 'FOR ANYONE'), a double bar with number keys and an ALT legend, and tape rows with no aligned facts column.
The rail-legend grammar holds, but it is the weakest of the carried breeds: an olive-fill setup tray, glowing bubble edges spreading the light, tracked caps legends, and Status still boxed cards.

A rich instrument language (readout strip, flight-plan arcs, crew board), undone by tracked caps nav and keys, 23 small targets, an annunciator that repeats the Status lists, and FIG captions that tell the family nothing.

Coherent as a teletext service: a page number for every view, one double-height headline per page, and a mosaic drawing leading each section. But it is loud. VT323 at 25px sits off the glass, section hues fill whole bands, controls are in caps (EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE; FILTER), 46 of 56 Home targets are small, and the tall-tick apostrophe shows at headline size.

Home's dome, with Vera at the zenith and plans as stars, is a lovely picture, and Chat's meridian thread with maroon family bubbles works. The system does not carry: the other pages drop to generic cards with parchment serif titles and italic decks, a teal ground and pills. The stars are unlabelled, and 40 targets are small.
Its child supersedes it. The brown case, VT323 band heads, pastel number tiles, nav moved to a foot key row and a 3574px Home still stand.

Bold and warm, but not a standard for daily use. Ransom-letter titles are hard to read, masking tape on every scrap is noise, and red marker loops for 'here' sit beside red 'late' scrawls. The one-size type flattens every page, and the grain and tear masks are heavy to paint. The glow showing through torn holes is the idea worth keeping.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the template: terminal = tube + deck + contents plate + status foot; desk = square matte bands of one-line rows with column heads and ringed numbers. Fix: (1) make the terminal position:sticky with max-height:calc(100vh - bar) and NO inner scroll; move the For and Status banks to one latched row at the desk's head (the Kind bank can stay, set 3-up with icon + short word), so the Ideas terminal fits 900px. (2) On Home, widen the terminal to about 27rem or let the ways to start sit in one row of short keys under the box; the chips should not wrap to two rows. (3) Give every page's tube a job so the rule holds everywhere: the form's tube prints the new idea's row as it is typed, Family's shows who is signed in as lamps, Wishes' shows each kid's open count, and an idea's page shows its drive on the radar. Where nothing is live, collapse the terminal to its status foot as a strip above the desk rather than a box over an empty column. (4) Settings: keep the rows with their states on the desk, and let the deck show only the Contents stops, not a second list of pages. (5) Put the tube and foot after the list in DOM order on the phone, not CSS order. (6) Lighten Send's double focus ring to one 2px ring and a halo. Set the straight apostrophe on the glass.

Carry the head-column figure, the column heads and the NOW marker into the standard. Fix: drop the repeated long date in Coming up (keep the '1 OCT THU' chip and the time and relative day). Give Status bands the full measure, two-up where rows are short, and hang the spend tube in its head column. Make the row afterglow a steel or sage wash only, never amber, so it is not read as a selection or a warning. Make the Next up trace pulses taller and label the next one on the glass. Replace the 212px portrait radar with a square scope and the text below it.

Breed it with r12-idea-1 and do not carry both. Take the afterglow from the page head's lit tile as the page-level light rule. Fill Next up's blank glass with idea-1's four-week trace rather than a blank line before the prompt. Tie the afterglow's anchor to a token set by the head column, not to the listing's hard-coded widths.

Graft the instrument vocabulary (the lit dial for what is live, printed registers and meters for what is past) and the lead-and-hairline divider into the leader's Status and Settings. Fix: flatten the register wheels to printed tabular figures in a recessed window. Show the limit and a ghost maximum on the dial so a zero reading still says something. Keep the sweep beam off the words. Give Status's lamp tables the full row width so cells don't wrap.

Keep the rack module, the contents line as the one head drawing, and the prompt typed on the glass. Fix: sentence-case every control (Add an idea, Send, Tell Vera something). Let cells size to their content (grid-auto-rows:min-content, and span tall cells) so Memory and Wishes are not empty boxes. Set lists inside cells as one-line rows to a facts column, not the Ideas and To do cards. Keep the page-key row on Home too, and keep brass to the page numbers.

Keep the rule 'quote one thing large, tape the next few, the rest a key away' on every page, with the figure in the section's colour. Fix: swap the plum-graphite surfaces for neutral or green-black slate. Keep mono caps to column heads and legends, never inline facts or controls. Drop the visible ALT legend and the number keys from the bar, since they collide with access keys. Align the tape rows to one tabular facts column. Set To do's quoted task at the title step, not larger.

Keep the page numbers as the bar's index and a mosaic drawing per section. Fix: VT323 for page headlines and numbers only. Section colour as a rule and an icon, not band fills. Sentence-case controls at 44px targets. Labels at a 13-14px step, not 25px.

Keep the tube glowing up through a torn hole: one per page, where the machine is live. Set titles in type rather than cut-out letters, allow at most one strip of tape per page, and keep red for late alone, with steel for 'here'.

Keep Home's chart dome with Vera at the zenith, but label the plan stars and give their angle a meaning (days out). Use sans titles and upright decks, set the ground neutral black, and hold the chart vocabulary (hour ring, coordinates) on Plans and Chat so the system does not stop at Home.

Graft the width-axis rule (narrow for large titles, normal for what is read, wide only for the tiny labels) and the slashed zero onto the listing leader. Keep labels in mono at .72rem, not wide caps, so the date stays below her name.

judges.notes:
Through a system lens this round splits in two: entrants that define how a page is built, and entrants that restyle a page.

Desk Terminal (r12-idea-2) is the first to state a page template the whole app could be built from. Machine things live in one cased, rounded, lit column: the tube, the latched keys, the contents plate and the status foot. Family things live on a square, matte desk of one-line rows. That turns principle 13 (only the machine is rounded) and 19 (light is a list) into layout, and it brings back the original tube's warm-up and bloom in exactly one place per page. It isn't finished: the column needs a job on every page, no inner scroll, and a roomier composer on Home.

Evening Listing, Traced (r12-idea-1) is the most complete version of the proven listing grammar. A head-column figure, column heads, and a NOW marker inside the list are all rules I would write into the standard today. The strongest next breed is Desk Terminal's machine column over Traced's desk, with Afterglow's page-head light and Metered's printed instruments on Status.

Afterglow and Relit are near-duplicates, so carry only one.

The wild lane's best ideas are structural: Switchboard's rack module with a contents line as the single head drawing, and Single Quote's 'one thing large' hierarchy. Both lose on the same held rules as before: caps on controls, tinted grounds, empty or stretched cells, and legends with no facts column.

Controls are sound across the leaders: filled fields with a green ring, square ticks, steel-latched selects. Afterglow on hover is still near-invisible in every details strip, now the fourth round.

Today scores 4.4 through this lens; the best entrant scores 8.5.

scores.why: Yardstick. The lit greeting gives a clear first action, but 45 of 57 Home targets are under 44px. On Ideas the radar pushes every idea below the fold. To do cards repeat 'Edit, complete, or snooze' four times, and late is never shown on the To do page.

Changes how every page works, not only how it looks. Filters on Ideas, To do and Plans are one-tap latched keys with a visible LED state, one control per filter. A status foot on every page says whether Vera works and what she costs. The Contents plate and the To do tube (Late / This week / Later / No date) read at a glance. All 12 ideas are above the fold, there are 0 small targets on every page, and Home is about 1450px. What it loses: on inner pages the lit tube and its controls come before the h1 in the sight line and in the DOM, so title-then-action is weaker, and the Contents plate repeats the band heads.

The listing's clarity with real fixes. There is one kind filter (two-up, the select dropped), WHO/DUE and STATE column heads, big head-column figures, '2 late' as a link, and a NOW divider that splits late from upcoming on Home and To do. 'Edit' replaces the repeated sentence, and every page has 0 small targets. It loses points for a To do search squeezed into the head column (placeholder cut off, icon-only button), dates repeated in Coming up, a Next up trace that reads as a barcode, and a harness-hover row that looks selected.

Still a very legible system: head columns that state how each band stands, one-line rows to tabular facts, steel reverse for 'here', words in the bar, 0 small targets. The kind list and the Kind select still duplicate each other, To do's search sits apart from its Show list, and the row afterglow is invisible.

Works the same as Relit, which is good. The afterglow haze and the prompt line on Next up change the light, not how the page is used or read, and the new Next up leaves about 40px of blank glass between the date and the prompt.

Home's tables with column heads and right-aligned figures are quick to scan, and the To do tube shows late on a timeline. Status's three narrow tables wrap each row to three or four lines, and Ideas still has both the All/Restaurants tabs and a Kind select.

The Status meters add a glanceable read of spend and cache. At $0.00 both needles rest at zero, the number-wheel register is obscure to a family, and all of it is aria-hidden. Everywhere else it works as its parent does, with rules that lengthen Home.

Lines with order help (Coming up track, the To do timetable with amber lamps). Memory, Family, Status and Settings are icons only in the bar, and the To do page drops the 'was due' words, so late is shown by colour and position only.

Fixes Flight Console's usability: 0 small targets, sentence-case nav, amber 'Was due' and edges on To do, and a readout strip that doubles as links. It costs comprehension in other ways: Status is caps annunciator tiles that are harder to read than rows, 'CONSOLE 03 | TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY' costume, the flight-plan arcs repeat the Coming up rows, and Home is about 2100px.

The Home switchboard is the round's best answer to 'find what you came for'. Every page is a cell whose head is a 44px key with a count, and ticks, lamps and the settings index sit right on Home. But the cells carry equal weight, so the squint loses priority, and the question sits at the foot of a tall tube below Next up. Controls are tracked caps. To do's Show/Search are below the fold under the tube. Home lacks the page row the other pages have, and 8 to 20 targets per page are under 44px.
A clear state system (rail legends, reverse video). Four bar places are icons only, the Chat puts everyone on the left, and the To do page has no late words.

Same interaction as its parent. The condensed titles sharpen the heads a little, but the wide caps labels now rival the names they label (the date beside 'Vera'), and the slashed VT323 zero blurs at Next up's size.

The strongest title-to-figure hierarchy of the round ('Ideas 12', 'Things to do 4 open'). It adds a one-line filter summary chip that states the filter's state, numbered access keys for keyboard users, and a Chat whose last line is set large. Failings: 53 of 59 Home targets and 28 of 29 on Status are under 44px, the tape rows are tiny tracked mono caps, it has two header rows of chrome, the To do page shows no late state, and the To do quote sets whichever task is first due huge.
The readout strip gives a real at-a-glance view, but the nav and links are tracked caps, 23 Home targets are under 44px, and the annunciator repeats the Status lists.

The centred Home has the cleanest single sight line of the round (Vera, the question, Send), and the Chat splits family and Vera well. Against that: round tick rings read as radio buttons, four bar places are icons only, the plan stars are unlabelled decoration, setup falls below the fold, 40 Home targets are under 44px, and the select focus is not green.

The squint is the clearest of the round: double-height headline, section-colour bands, page numbers as an index. But 46 of 56 Home targets are under 44px, the 25px VT323 dates in Coming up outrank the plan names, VT323 caps controls ('EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE') read as labels, and late is missing on To do.
Numbered Contents and the question on glass are good comprehension devices. On the desktop the nav moves to a key row at the foot, 35 Home targets are under 44px, and Home is about 3574px.

The red marker loop makes 'here' unmistakable, and setup sits above the fold. But the ransom-letter titles, including 'What's on your mind?', are slow to read, and the one-size type flattens dense pages. The label-tape caps controls ('SAVE A THOUGHT FOR LATER') look like labels, tape and torn edges add noise, 11 to 21 targets per page are under 44px, and the focused select has no green ring.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the terminal, the latched filter keys with LEDs, the status foot on every page, the To do tube's Late/This week/Later/No date bars and the warm-up from a line. Fix the sight line: put the page title (icon, h1, lede and the green primary) in a head row that spans desk and terminal, or first inside the terminal above the tube, so both the eye and the DOM go title, then action, then tube, then filters. Show the Contents plate only where a page has four or more bands, and on Settings keep either the deck bank or the rows with their states, not both. On pages with nothing live (form, Wishes, Family, Memory, an idea's page), fold the terminal into a one-line status foot under the title instead of an empty column. On the phone, move the tube in the DOM rather than with CSS order, so Tab order matches the drawing. Put Ideas' Status keys behind a disclosure or set them three-up, so the terminal ends inside 900px. Show the row highlight only on :hover with a pointer, and fade it over 1.2s so it never rests as a 'selected' state.

Keep the two-up kind filter as the only kind control, the WHO/DUE/STATE heads, '2 late' as a link and the NOW divider. Move To do's search to the top of the main column at full width, with a worded 'Search' button, or widen it to the full head column; today its placeholder is cut off and the button is an icon. In Coming up, drop either the day chip or the long date. Label the next pulse on the Next up trace and make the pulses taller, or the trace reads as a barcode. Make the row afterglow a visible 12% steel wash with a 2px sage edge that fades over about 1s (fourth round invisible). The 'Edit' key should say what it opens (for example 'Edit or snooze').

Keep the Home switchboard (every page a cell headed by a 44px key with a count and its live contents). It is the best 'where is everything' device yet, and it could be grafted as Home's lower half in the leader. Fix: set every control in sentence case (Add an idea, Send, Earlier). Put the question and the box at the top of the glass, with Next up under it, so the one action comes first. Give the needs-a-look cell (setup) the first and widest slot so equal cells still rank. Keep the page key row on Home too, for one nav everywhere. Move To do's Show/Search above its tube so filtering is on the first screen. Collapse near-empty cells (Memory, Restaurants, the Status plate). Give the select a green focus ring. Bring the Settings index rows and the Ideas cards' links to 44px.

Keep the quote figure beside each title, the one-line filter summary chip (graft it into the leader's Ideas and To do), the playscript Chat with its last line large, and the Status lamp strip ('6 working, 7 off'). Fix the targets: pad every tape row and see-more link to 44px, and set 'for anyone' and speakers in sentence-case sans at 0.9rem instead of tracked mono caps. Merge the command line and the key row into one bar, and show the number hints only on focus or with a '?' key rather than an ALT⇧ legend. Show late in amber on the To do page (the views.task_row late flag). Choose the To do quote by lateness, not by list order.

Keep the double-height headline, the section band and the page numbers as a quiet index. They give the clearest squint hierarchy of the round. Set dates and times in Plex Mono at row size so plan names lead. Make controls sentence-case sans buttons ('Edit or snooze', 'Filter'), not VT323 caps. Reach 0 targets under 44px, add amber late on To do, and drop the numbers from the bar below 1280px rather than hiding them.

Keep the centred sight line (Vera, the question, Send) and the family-right, Vera-left Chat. Use square tick boxes, put words on all nine bar places, and number the plan stars to match the Coming up rows, or drop them. Bring setup above the fold. Raise the bar and section links to 44px, and use a green focus ring on selects.

Keep the readout strip as a global row of 44px links and the amber late edges on To do. Set the Status tiles as sentence-case rows with lamps, not caps annunciator tiles. Drop the 'CONSOLE nn' captions and either the flight-plan arcs or the Coming up rows. Cut Home toward 1600px.

The red marker loop for 'here' is worth keeping. Set the question and titles in real type; ransom letters could at most be a small decoration beside a set h1. Make every control a sentence-case button rather than label tape, give the select a green focus ring, and bring small targets to 0.

judges.notes: Seen through this lens, the round splits into two groups. Some entrants changed how pages are used: Desk Terminal's latched filter keys and status foot, Traced's single filter and late link, Switchboard's page map, Single Quote's filter summary and access keys. Others changed only how pages look. The first group scored higher wherever they kept 0 small targets. Every wild entrant except Switchboard (8 to 20 per page) still fails the 44px rule badly: Single Quote 53 of 59 on Home, Ceefax 46, Zenith 40. That, not their ideas, is what holds them down. Recurring comprehension faults: (1) Tracked caps or VT323 caps on controls, which read as labels (Switchboard, Ceefax, Zine, Slate Flight Console's Status tiles). (2) The select focus ring missing on Switchboard, Zine and Zenith. (3) Late missing from the To do page (Single Quote, Ceefax, Switchboard, the Signal pair); only Desk Terminal, Traced, Relit, Afterglow, Long Persistence and Slate Flight Console show it in words. (4) The row afterglow is visible only on Switchboard and the Zine; in the listing family it is still invisible for a fourth round, and where a highlight does show it reads as a selected state. (5) Putting a lit tube top left before the h1 (Desk Terminal, Switchboard) wins the glance but costs the 'title first' sight line and Tab order. A head row spanning the page solves both. Tab order matches the drawing in every entrant on the desktop. Desk Terminal, Switchboard and Ceefax put Next up's links before the box, which is consistent with their layouts. On the phone, Desk Terminal's CSS-order swap is the one known mismatch. The breed this lens would write into the standard: Traced's listing rows and head-column figures, Desk Terminal's latched filter keys, status foot and To do tube, Single Quote's filter summary chip and quote figure beside the title, and Switchboard's map as the lower half of Home.

scores.why: Yardstick. One sans at a narrow range of small sizes, bold heads with little contrast in step, ISO dates set in body text on To do ('Due 2026-09-27 19:56'), and no tabular facts column anywhere. It is legible but flat, and nothing in it is set as a table.

The most complete type system here, and it shows on every page. Condensed Instrument Sans heads sit over Plex body. Each head column carries a big numeral over a small caps label ('4 / PLANS', '12 / IDEAS', '3 / ON · 1 OFF'). Column heads (WHO, DUE, DRIVE, WAY, FOR, #) have right-aligned tabular mono figures, and the date sub-columns are properly set, with weekday right-aligned, day on the digit and month left. Faults: the head-column notes wrap at about 20 characters, and the date column repeats the day chip.

A disciplined listing: dotted leaders run to fixed Time and 'in N days' sub-columns, WHO/DUE and DRIVE/FOR/# heads sit over tabular figures, all 12 ideas show on one screen, and VT323 stays on the glass. It loses some hierarchy because page titles are only about 2rem next to their icon, the months in 'Thu 1 Oct' are in denim link colour on text that is not a link, and drive and direction share one column.

The parent of the listing system: condensed heads, right-aligned date numerals with stacked OCT/THU mono caps, leaders to tabular facts, and a head column that states how things stand. It is well made, but its head-column states ('4 more / next in 2 days' in mono) are less systematic than its Traced child's figure-over-label.

The boldest typographic idea that works. Every head is a quote: a condensed Archivo title, then the section's figure in its colour, then a stacked mono legend ('Ideas 12 IN ALL / LAST ADDED SUN 27 SEP'). The Status lamp row reads '6 working 7 off', and Settings are numbered 0·1 to 0·9. What lets it down: mono caps set inline in rows ('Pho Oregon FOR ANYONE', 'SAM', 'YESTERDAY'), a first To do row set at about 36px so row sizes are unequal, the chat's last line upsized, and tape text at 12-14px.

True column heads (DAY PLAN TIME IN, LAMP WHAT STATE) over right-aligned tabular figures, with condensed titles. It reads like a well-set ledger. But the Status tables are squeezed into thirds, so cells wrap to three lines, and the list heads ('The list') are small.

Typographically this is its parent. The one change is that Next up's date drops to the tube's small VT323 step, below the prompt line, and leaves about 40px of blank glass, which is a small step back in hierarchy on the glass.

Long Persistence's good tables, with instrument figures added. The register's number wheels and the meter scales set tiny numerals ('0.50', '1.00', '25 50 75') that are ornament, not reading, and the Status lamp tables still wrap to three lines.

One superfamily with clear jobs: Plex Sans Condensed heads, Plex Sans text, and Plex Mono readouts with zero-padded figures on dotted leaders ('PLANS ........ 05'). Heads carry inline mono meta ('4 open · 2 late'), and the nav is back in sentence case. It still has FIG. captions and Status caps plates, and 'Mount St. Helens day / trip' wraps in the four-card row.

The only entrant that changes type and nothing else, and the idea is elegant: one variable face whose width axis carries the hierarchy. The 70% condensed titles improve on the parent's clunky Plex Bold, and zeros are slashed. The execution is weak: Archivo at 400 body weight is paler than Plex, the 115% wide caps date now competes with Vera's name, and at page scale the change is subtle.

Clean condensed heads, and the timetable margin hangs due times in mono, which is good sequence typesetting on To do and Chat. Otherwise it is a card layout without a facts column, and its small grey meta lines are similar to today's.

The sommaire contents line (lamp, page number, name, dotted leader, count) is a true pagination device, and Settings list 991-999 as a numbered contents. But narrow cells wrap titles ('Call the dentist about / Theo', 'Silver / Falls hike'), the tracked caps buttons ('+ ADD AN IDEA') shout, and the page numbers are tiny beside 46px plate titles.

A refined atlas setting: Source Serif titles and names, caps section heads led by Greek letters (α COMING UP), and red mono coordinates. It is coherent and pretty, but it pulls off the CRT. The italic decks and italic ways-to-start chips slow reading, and every serif item title is underlined, so all of them read as links.
Plex Sans with mono caps rail legends, which is serviceable. Heads in Plex Bold are heavy at the larger steps, and the rows have no aligned facts column.

Page numbers in the bar and the headers (P100, 200, 300) are real pagination, and each view has one strong headline. But VT323 stretched to double height for every headline and section head, 25px VT323 dates, labels and attributions (loud on the phone), and the tall apostrophe move the pixel face off the glass and onto the whole page. That is costume more than setting.
Zero-padded readouts are a good figure treatment. But the nav and 'ALL →' links are tracked mono caps, the CONSOLE 02 | CAPCOM eyebrows and FIG. captions are tiny noise, and the body steps are small.
VT323 band titles, all-caps nav, caps buttons and key rows, and Martian Mono labels add up to too many shouting voices. Its large numbered item titles are its one strong move.

The ransom-note titles are illegible as setting ('W H A T ' S  O N'). The one-size rule removes the hierarchy, and it uses five faces (Space Mono, Bricolage Grotesque, Archivo, Victor Mono script, Fraunces). The handwritten 'in 2 days' is charming but only as an accent.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the whole system: figure over caps label in every head column, the WHO/DUE/DRIVE/WAY/FOR/# heads, the date sub-columns set on the digit, and condensed heads over Plex. Fix the measure: the head-column prose ('Google Calendar is not connected...') wraps at about 20 characters to five lines, so move it to a foot line under the rows or widen the column to 13rem. Drop either the day chip's month/weekday or the long 'Thursday 1 October' column, and keep the chip, then time, then relative. Set the head numeral on the same baseline as the first row. On Status, let the 44rem facts run to the band's edge instead of leaving about 230px empty.

Raise page titles to the listing's condensed display step (about 2.5-2.75rem) so they outrank band heads. Set the month in 'Thu 1 Oct' in ink or label colour, since denim should mean a link. Split drive and direction into DRIVE and WAY columns as Traced does. Keep the Contents plate with leaders to counts, which is excellent pagination.

Keep the quote head (condensed title, section figure in its colour, stacked two-line mono legend) and the 0·1-0·9 numbering, and make them the standard head for every page. Fix the rows: never set mono caps inline in a row ('FOR ANYONE', 'SAM', 'YESTERDAY'), and use sentence-case label ink in a facts column instead. Keep every row on To do and Chat the same size, since the 'quote' belongs in the head, not in a 36px first row or an enlarged last chat line. Raise the tape to a 15px step with tabular figures.

Keep the width axis as the hierarchy: 70% titles, 80% rail heads, 100% text. Set the text at Archivo 420-440 (or keep Plex Sans for long text) so body copy is not paler. Bring the wide caps labels down to about 105-108% width and .04em tracking so the date stops competing with Vera's name. Carry the slashed zero into the facts columns too.

Keep the contents line (lamp · page number · name · leader · count) and the numbered Settings contents, since that pagination is the idea. Drop the plate title step from 46px to about 32px so titles stop breaking in a 285px column. Widen the To do cell or give it a one-line row with a WHO/DUE column so titles stop wrapping. Set buttons in sentence case, and put page numbers at the label step on the head's baseline.

Keep page numbers in the bar and headers (a real pagination system) and one double-height headline per view. Keep VT323 to that headline and the glass, and set section heads in a condensed sans. Set dates and '[IN 2 DAYS]' in the reading face with tabular figures, and drop the 25px VT323 labels on the phone to a 13-14px mono.

If the atlas serif returns, set the decks and chips in roman, not italic. Underline only item titles that are links, and not every catalogue entry. Keep the Greek-letter section heads and the red coordinate mono, which are its best typographic moves.

Replace the cut-out ransom letters with one display face at a real title step, and bring back at least three sizes. Keep the Victor Mono script for 'was due' annotations only, and cut the faces to three.

judges.notes: The Evening Listing family is still the best typesetting on the panel, and Traced is its best form. It has a numeral over a small-caps label in every head column, column heads over right-aligned tabular mono facts, dates set on the digit in fixed sub-columns, leaders only where a fact follows, and condensed Instrument Sans heads over Plex. That could be written into the standard as it is. Desk Terminal reaches almost the same table setting but gives up title hierarchy. Two new typographic ideas are worth breeding into the leader. The first is Single Quote's quote head: title, then the section figure, then a stacked legend. It would replace the head column's figure on narrow screens and gives Plans, To do and Settings a figure in the title line. The second is Videotex Switchboard's contents line with page numbers, which is pagination the owner would enjoy. Signal Legend, Widths shows that a single variable face can carry a scale by width. It is subtle at page scale, so it is better grafted onto the listing than carried alone. Recurring faults, again: mono or tracked caps set inline in rows or on buttons, VT323 used off the glass (Ceefax, Videotex), italic decks (Zenith), and one-size or ransom titles (Glow Ink Zine). Head-column prose is set to about 20 characters in the listing children, which is too narrow a measure. Measures: the leaders all hold 0 small targets on Home. The wild entrants with the most typographic character (Ceefax 46/56, Zenith 40/56, Single Quote 53/59) are also the ones with the most small targets.

scores.why: Every filter works the same way: one-tap latched keys for Kind, For and Status on Ideas, Open, Done, Cancelled and All on To do, and List/Month and Earlier/Later on Plans. So Restaurants, overdue and a month are one click each. The To do tube counts Late 2, This week, Later and No date; 'was due' is in amber words; the numbered bands and the Contents plate give counts, with '2 late' as a link. The bar has words, no target is under 44px, row text is about 17px, and Home fits in about 1.5 screens. Costs: Home's message box is narrow in the terminal column, the Ideas terminal scrolls inside itself at 900px, the phone's Tab order no longer follows the layout (CSS order), and a pencil alone hides 'complete, or snooze'.

This fixes the leader's two faults. There is now one kind filter, set two-up in the head column (the duplicate Kind select is gone), and '2 late' is a link. To do and Status get WHO/DUE/STATE column heads, and a NOW marker in the To do list splits overdue from coming up. Still to fix: Status and For stay as selects behind a Filter button beside the one-click kind keys. The '?late=1' link needs a route change. 'Edit' replaced 'Edit, complete, or snooze'. The portrait radar wraps at about 17 characters, and the hover afterglow left on a setup row reads as a selection.

Usability is the same as Evening Listing, Relit: head columns that say how each band stands, amber 'was due' on Home and To do, Open/Done/Cancelled/All as navigation, words in the bar and no small targets. The returned afterglow over each page title helps show where you are and costs nothing. It keeps the parent's faults: two kind filters on Ideas (the list and the Kind select), a '2 late' that is not a link, and the date given twice in Coming up.

Still one of the easiest pages to use: head columns, one-line rows with tabular facts, amber late words on both Home and To do, and the bar in words. Its own children now fix its duplicate kind filter (Traced) or match it with the light back (Afterglow).

Tables with column heads let tired eyes scan one column, Home is short, late shows in amber words on Home and To do, and the To do tube says '2 LATE'. The sweep beam still crosses Next up's words, the scope bars have no key, and To do's Show is still a select plus a Filter button.

Everything that works in the parent is kept. The new Status instruments ask more decoding than words do: a '001.26' odometer, a needle resting at 0 and split bars. They repeat the spend sentence and push the lamp tables below the fold. The rule between bands is harmless.

A real gain on Flight Console: the nav is in sentence-case words with Home, and there are 0 small targets. The readout strip (PLANS 05, TO DO 04, LATE 02 in amber) is the fastest glance in the round, and To do cards say 'Was due' in amber. The costume still costs comprehension: HOLDS, T-3/T-2, 'Console 09 | Systems', 'Capcom' and FIG captions. Status becomes a grid of tiny caps cells that are harder to read than a list, Coming up starts at 2, the kids' wishes sit at the foot, and Home is about 2100px.
The Coming up track and the timetable chat are clear. But the right side of the bar is still icons only, and the To do page shows late by colour and position alone, with no 'was due' words.
The ruled trays are readable and Home says WAS DUE. The To do page shows only dates, the right side of the bar is icons, and the glowing bubble edges make every message look equally live.

It is the same page as Signal Legend Relit for every task. The condensed titles read well, but the slashed VT323 zero blooms into an '8' at Next up's size ('17:00'), and the wide caps labels compete with names. The icon-only right bar and the unmarked late on To do remain.
The readout strip is a good glance. The nav is tiny tracked caps, Home has 23 small targets, and HOLDS, T-minus and FIG are jargon. Its mutant, Slate Flight Console, now does all of this better.

Home as a map of every page, each with a count and a lamp, is a strong way to see what is where, and the To do boxes are 44px. But Home has no page-tab row while every other page does. On Ideas the search and kind filters sit below the radar and off the first screen, so 'show only restaurants' means hunting. Idea cards are tall and half empty (9 to a screen). The message is typed in green VT323 on the glass, so the box reads as display text. To do does not mark late, and ADD AN IDEA is in tracked caps.

The large serif reads easily at night. Home shows plans, to-dos and the box on one screen, and Chat puts Vera on the left and the family in maroon on the right, so speakers are clear. Costs: Finish setting up drops below the fold, and the round to-do ticks look like radio buttons. The plan stars on the dome are unlabelled decoration, the right side of the bar is icons only, Home has 40 small targets, and To do does not mark late.

The bar names every page in words, the Ideas filter pill shows its current state, and each title's figure plus change line ('Ideas 12, last added Sun 27 Sep') is a good glance. But Home has 53 of 59 targets under 44px, the worst here. The first task on To do is set as a headline as if it were special, and late is not marked. Show is folded behind a disclosure, the numbered access keys may clash with a screen reader, and the tape's 12-14px caps are small.

The labels at 25px are big for tired eyes, the section colours help people find their way, and late is marked on Home. But Memory, Family, Status and Settings are an icon plus a number (600/700/800/890), links read 'ALL 4 400', and the double-height titles push content down. Controls are in VT323 caps ('EDIT, COMPLETE, OR SNOOZE'), To do does not mark late, and 46 of 56 Home targets are under 44px.

The Contents list with counts helps. But the main nav moves to a key row under the terminal, setup is last on a very long Home, 35 targets are small, and the message field is VT323 text inside the tube.

Yardstick. On Home, 45 of 57 targets are under 44px. The right side of the bar is icons only, the To do page does not mark late, the Ideas cards show two rows above the fold, and the contrast (17.1) is harsh at night. Everything can still be found.

The ransom-letter titles ('What's on your mind', 'Things to do', 'Sign in to FamilyDB') are slow to read, and setting every word at one 17px size removes the hierarchy a first-time user steers by. The Workbench face on the tube makes 'Pho Oregon' hard to read, and the tape overlaps the cards. The To do page has no late marking, 11 to 21 targets per page are small, and the right side of the bar is icons only.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the terminal, the one-tap latched keys everywhere, the To do tally tube, the numbered bands and the status foot. They are the most consistent controls in any round. Fixes: (1) On Home, give the message box the full desk width, or widen the terminal to about 34rem on Home only. Keep 'What's on your mind?' on the glass, but the field should be at least 3 rows and as wide as the bands. (2) Stop the Ideas terminal scrolling inside itself: make it sticky with the page doing the scrolling, or fold For and Status into a disclosure under Kind. (3) On the phone, reorder the DOM rather than using CSS order, so Tab matches the drawing. (4) Put the words back beside the pencil ('Edit or snooze'), or at least give it a visible label on hover and focus. (5) Make the tube's 'Late 2' row a link to the late filter, and ship views.task_row `late`. (6) Drop the 'On this page' plate when a page has five bands or fewer, and don't list the Settings pages twice. (7) Pages with nothing live (forms, Family, Memory) should use the full width, not show an empty terminal. (8) Let the row afterglow fade out completely so the parked mouse never looks like a selection.

Keep the single kind key, the '2 late' link, the column heads and the NOW marker in the To do list. Make Status and For one-click keys in the head column like Kind, so filtering works one way and the Filter button serves only the search. Ship the ?late=1 route. Restore 'Edit, complete, or snooze' (or 'Edit or snooze'). Widen the Ideas radar or put it back beside the filters, so it does not wrap at 17 characters. Put a key on the Next up trace ('a bar is a plan') and make each bar a link. Drop the repeated date in Coming up.

Keep the afterglow over each page title: it helps show where you are. Take the Kind select off Ideas, since the head-column list already filters by kind. Make '2 late' a link, and show one date per plan in Coming up. Fill Next up's blank glass under the date with the plan's place or a fortnight trace, or size the tube to its words.
Keep the tables. Run the sweep beam only below the text block, add a one-line key under each scope, and turn To do's Show select into Open/Done/All keys.
If the instruments stay, put the figure in words beside each one ('$1.26 in 30 days', 'none from the cache'), and keep the lamp tables above the fold by setting the instrument strip after them.

Keep the readout strip as 44px links and the amber 'Was due' on the To do cards. Rename HOLDS to Setup. Drop the T-3/T-2, Console/Capcom and FIG captions. Set Status as sentence-case rows with state words, not caps cells. Start Coming up at 1, and move the kids' wishes up to sit beside To do.

Keep Home as the service map with counts and lamps. Give Home the same page-tab row as every other page. On Ideas, put the search and a Kind/Restaurants bank at the top of column 1, under the plate and before the tube. Size cards to their content, with the pictogram inline, not in an empty corner. Make the message box a plain bone-ink field under the tube. Set buttons in sentence case, and mark late on To do.

Keep the figure-plus-change-line title and the words-and-numbers nav: it is the best 'how does this page stand' head in the round. Stop setting the first task as a headline, and put '2 late' in the change line in amber instead. Unfold Show into Open/Done/All keys. Give the tape links and 'All' links 44px targets. Mark late tasks amber on the To do page, and move Settings into the nav row.

Keep the serif, the one-screen Home and the two-sided chat. Move Finish setting up to the top while it has steps. Use square checkboxes for to-dos. Label the plan stars with their names, or make them links, or drop them. Put words on the right side of the bar, meet 44px targets, and mark late on To do.

Name Memory, Family, Status and Settings in words. Keep the page number only in the header, not inside every link. Set controls in sentence case in the reading face, mark late on To do, and give the inline links 44px targets.

Keep the torn-glass tubes and the red marker for late, and the tape as ornament. Set the question, the page titles and sign-in in real type; a single ransom strip on the page title alone is enough. Use a readable face on the tube, add at least one larger title step, mark late on To do, and put words on the right side of the bar.

judges.notes:
I walked each candidate's own pages through the family's tasks.

**Send Vera a message and read the reply.** It works everywhere.
- The listing family and Long Persistence give the widest, calmest box.
- Desk Terminal's Home box is the smallest of the leaders.
- Videotex (both) and Switchboard type the message in VT323 on the glass, so the box reads as display text.
- On Chat, Zenith Desk and Evening Listing make the speakers clearest (Vera left, the family right). Single Quote's flat transcript does not.

**See what is on this weekend.** Fastest are Desk Terminal's Contents plate, Evening Listing's head columns and Slate Flight Console's readout strip. Zenith's plan stars are unlabelled.

**Add an idea and find it again; show only the restaurants.**
- One click on Desk Terminal, Evening Listing Traced, Single Quote and the listing parents.
- Only Desk Terminal makes every Ideas filter one mechanism (latched links).
- On Switchboard the filters are below the first screen.

**Tick off a to-do and see what is overdue.** This task separates the field.
