- Late shows in amber words on the To do page itself in Desk Terminal (plus the Late 2 tally), Traced (plus the NOW divider and a '2 late' link), Afterglow and Relit, Long Persistence and Metered, and Slate Flight Console.
- The wild entrants all miss it.

**Find a date on Plans.** Fine everywhere. Desk Terminal and Slate Flight Console keep view and month keys together.

**Change a setting.** The bar is in words on the listing family, Long Persistence, Desk Terminal, Slate Flight Console, Single Quote and Switchboard. Signal Legend and Track Diagram are icon-only. Ceefax uses icons plus numbers.

**Sign in.** Fine everywhere except Glow Ink Zine's ransom title.

**Targets under 44px on Home.**
- 0 in the listing, persistence, signal and terminal families.
- 1 in Track Diagram.
- Worse than today in Single Quote (53) and Ceefax (46).
- 40 in Zenith, 11 in the Zine and 8 in Switchboard.

**Contrast and text size.** All entrants measure at least 4.8:1. The lowest are the Zine's dim tube lines (4.82) and Single Quote (4.89). The leaders sit at 5.3-5.5 with ink at about 12.5, which is gentler at night than today's 17.1.

**Removals.**
- Traced dropping the Kind select is a gain. Its 'Edit' for 'Edit, complete, or snooze' costs snooze's discoverability, and Desk Terminal's pencil costs the same.
- Single Quote folding Show and Switchboard pushing the filters down both lose one-glance tasks.

**The owner's test.** Every leader changes Home below the fold, Chat, Ideas, Status and To do, not a corner. Desk Terminal changes the most while staying the easiest.

**The rules a usability judge would add to the standard:**
- Each page has one place for its controls, and every filter there is a one-tap latched key.
- Late is amber words on Home and To do, plus a count that links to the filtered list.
- The bar names every place in words.
- No target is under 44px.
- Hover light fades to nothing.

Today scores 5.0. The best this round, Desk Terminal, scores 9.0.

scores.why: The yardstick. It is green on black all over (83% green share), with neon kind words, the same card on every section and one layer of glow on everything. It is the Matrix the family named, though its tube light is still the best-made thing on the page.

This is the only newcomer whose change shows on every page: one cased terminal at the left holds the single lit tube at full bloom, the controls and a status foot, and the matte slate desk beside it holds the family's rows. Faults: the greeting's big question has become a small VT323 line on the glass (with a stray high apostrophe), so Home's largest heading is now 'Finish setting up'. The Contents plate repeats the band heads. 'Oct' in denim reads as a link. Status links to itself from its own foot. The Ideas filter bank fills the whole viewport.

The best refinement of the leader. It has one kind filter (the select is gone), column heads, a figure in each head column, a lit NOW lamp between To do rows and plain 'Edit'. Faults: the hovered setup row is an amber-bronze fill that reads as selected. The Next up trace is a tiny barcode. Coming up still prints '1 OCT THU' beside 'Thursday 1 October'. The Ideas scope is squeezed into a narrow portrait tube.

The column-headed tables and tubes that draw the family's own weeks, dues and spend still hold up, and the tube light stays on its short list. Faults: To do's tube is mostly empty glass with two spikes. Status squeezes three tables until every cell wraps. The Ideas and Plans heads leave dead black to the right.

The boldest structural change that still works. Home is a graphite switchboard of every page, the question is typed on a big lit tube, and section colour is only a 2px cap and a number, which is truly grounded. Faults: page numbers (200, 310, 991) are costume the family never uses. Several cells stand half empty (Memory, Restaurants). The keys are tracked caps ('ADD AN IDEA'). To do's three card columns wrap every title. The nav sits in two places.

Still calm and well lit, but its own child now beats it on every point, so carrying both wastes a slot. Ideas still lists Restaurants twice (the kind list and the Kind select), and To do repeats 'Edit, complete, or snooze' on every row.

The Status meters are a real addition, but the needle rests at zero and reads as decoration, and the register's wheels lean skeuomorphic. Home, Chat, Ideas and To do differ from the parent only by a thin rule: a near-duplicate everywhere but Status.

A clear improvement on Flight Console: grounded slate, visible banding, sentence-case links and amber painted with one job. Costume survives: zero-padded '05' readouts, HOLDS, T-3/T-2/T-1, faint FIG captions and 'CONSOLE 03 | TARGETS OF OPPORTUNITY'. Square dots have replaced the nav icons, and Home is still about 2100px long.

This is literally 'a wash in the corner': a faint scanlined green haze behind each page title on an otherwise identical parent. It is a near-duplicate, the duplicated kind filter is unfixed, and the light lands on the page title, which is not live.
The lit track from the now lamp is a good idea. But the setup tray is still an olive-bronze fill, cards sit inside cards, and at page scale it reads as today with lines added.

The best type of the round: big condensed titles each carrying their figure in the section colour ('Ideas 12', 'Things to do 4'), a compact three-column Home board and setup cut to one line. Faults: a plum cast on every surface, a second bar row of ALT access keys, 53 small targets, tracked violet mono caps on every legend, a one-sided log for Chat, and still an 88% green share.

This is a typesetting-only mutant, so the page looks the same as its parent. The olive-bronze setup tray remains, the wide caps labels are louder than the names they label, and the slashed zero blurs '$0.00' and '17:00' on the glass.
The olive-bronze setup tray, glowing edges on Vera's chat bubbles (light spread onto things that are not live) and neon kind words (38% of the colour that is not green) keep it behind its successors.

Putting Vera at the centre of Home with everything in orbit is a genuinely new composition. But the ground is visibly night-teal rather than black, and it uses a starfield and a serif (both lost before), Greek-letter costume on the section heads, and maroon family bubbles that read as warnings.
Tracked mono caps nav and 'ALL →' links, 'CONSOLE 09 | SYSTEMS' costume, an annunciator that repeats the Status lists, and a one-sided Chat.

Coherent, and the whole page changes, but it is the loudest entrant, not a calmer one. VT323 is set double height on every head with a tall stray apostrophe, the To do head band is olive, it has 46 small targets and a bar full of page numbers, and the phosphor has no spark left when every head is a pixel face.
A brown plastic case (the bronze trap), olive-khaki mosaic head bands, VT323 titles, pastel tiles on the nav moved to a foot key row, and a 3500px Home.

This is a costume: ransom-note titles that must be spelled out letter by letter, a grey card ground rather than black, brown card scraps, masking tape, and red marker used for here, today and late, which turns 'today' into an alarm. The torn hole that shows the tube is its one good idea.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the terminal column, the single lit tube at full strength, the status foot and the matte square desk; that is the system. Fix: (1) Give Home its headline back, either the question in the sans display step above the box (with 'mind' lit) or on the glass at about 2rem with a straight apostrophe. (2) Keep the Contents plate only where it adds a figure the band heads lack, and drop the numbered rings on the bands. (3) Set month abbreviations in bone, keeping denim for links alone. (4) Hide the foot's 'Status →' on the Status page. (5) On Ideas, keep Kind as the two-up bank and fold For and Status into a disclosure so the terminal ends above the fold. (6) On pages with nothing live, shrink the terminal to its foot and let the desk go full width.

Keep the single kind filter, the column heads, the head-column figures and the lit NOW lamp between rows. Fix: make the setup hover a 10-14% steel wash with a sage edge, never an amber fill. Either make the Next up trace taller with the next plan labelled on the glass, or drop it. Remove the long-date column in Coming up, since the day chip already carries the date. Put the Ideas scope back in landscape beside the list.

Size To do's tube to its data or fill it with the fortnight trace. On Status, give each table the full width in turn instead of three wrapped thirds. Put a head-column figure beside the page titles so the right side is not dead black.

Keep the switchboard Home, the graphite modules, the 2px section caps and the question on the lit glass. Drop the page numbers everywhere except as a quiet contents index, if at all. Set the keys in sentence case. Let empty cells collapse (span Memory and Restaurants into their neighbours). Make To do a one-line list, not three cramped cards. Use one nav: the top bar, with no second tab row.

Keep the condensed title with its figure in the section colour, the three-column Home board and the one-line setup strip. Swap the plum housing for neutral graphite. Merge the ALT access-key row into the single bar and bring the targets up to 44px. Set the legends in bone sentence case instead of violet tracked mono. Give Chat back the family-on-the-right split.

Keep Vera at the centre of Home with the sections in orbit, and the plans as lamps, but label them. Put it on the true black ground, set names in the sans instead of the serif, drop the starfield and the Greek letters, and make the family's bubbles steel instead of maroon.

Keep the small mosaic drawings as page-head pictures and the flat grounded section colours. Keep VT323 on the glass only and set the heads in condensed sans at a single step. Drop the olive and brown head bands and the page numbers in the bar.
Take the afterglow off the page title (not live) and put it where the tube actually is. Fix the duplicated kind filter as Traced did. As it stands it is a corner wash on a near-duplicate.

Bring the Lucide icons back in the nav in place of the square dots. Drop HOLDS, the zero padding, the T-minus labels and the FIG captions. Make the readout strip a row of 44px links (Late goes to To do filtered). Keep the banding and the steel reverse for 'here'.

judges.notes: The owner's test of changes across the whole page separates the field. Desk Terminal, Videotex Switchboard, Single Quote, Ceefax, Zenith and the Zine change every page. Afterglow, Widths and Metered change almost nothing outside one area (Afterglow a haze behind the title, Widths the type, Metered the Status panel), so I scored them as near-duplicates of their parents. The Evening Listing family now has three members (Relit, Traced, Afterglow); carry Traced alone. Colour traps still present: an olive-bronze setup tray on Signal Legend, Widths and Track Diagram Relit, and an amber-bronze hover fill on Traced's setup row. Brown or olive surfaces appear on the Zine, Ceefax (To do band) and Videotex Sommaire. Tinted grounds appear on Zenith (teal) and Single Quote (plum). Red for 'today' and for late turns the Zine's calendar into an alarm. By the measures, a plum cast does not make Single Quote less monochrome (88.5% green share, above today's 83%), while Desk Terminal (55%) and Traced (56%) get their variety from grounded companions. VT323 off the glass lost again (Ceefax, Sommaire). The one faithful new use of the CRT is Switchboard's and Desk Terminal's question typed on the lit glass, but it costs Home its big typographic moment, so the next round should try both: the lit glass plus a sans headline step. Desk Terminal's terminal column is the idea most worth making the standard, because it gives every page (Plans, To do and Settings included) one place for the light and one for the family's rows.

designs.name: Signal Legend, Widths
designs.tagline: Signal Legend Relit reset in one variable face, Archivo, at three widths: narrow titles, normal text, and wide tiny capital labels, which are the only capitals left, with slashed zeros in the mono and on the glass.
designs.concept: This is Signal Legend Relit with only its typesetting changed. The whole page's words are now in one variable face, Archivo, and its width axis carries the hierarchy. The larger a title, the narrower it is set, so page titles and the greeting's question are 70% condensed, like a timetable, and rail heads are 80%. Everything that is read, pressed or typed is at normal width. The tiny labels are 115% wide, like an engraved nameplate, and they are now the page's only capitals. The machine's figures stay in Plex Mono, and the tube's stay in VT323, both switched to the period's slashed zero. The page reads calmer and more typeset while the parent's slate, steel and light stay exactly as they were.
designs.companions: Unchanged from the parent, r10-mut-5. Steel #a7c4d8 is the accent and link colour and the rail leads. Slate carries the trays, strips, bar and bezel. The reverse-video steel block marks "here". Bone ink (#d4cfc4) and heading (#ebe6da) carry the text, with a steel-blue label (#a4b0c2). The cobalt wash #4f60e6 sits at 2.5 in the greeting's corner. Exact #6dff9c is kept for the mark, "mind", Send, the lamps and the tubes, and sage #86d9a6 for lit and outing. This entrant changes no colour. The only colour-adjacent effect is that the wide caps labels show slightly more of the label steel, because their letters are broader.
decisions: MAJOR ROLL, width as hierarchy: --sans is Archivo, the variable face with wdth 62-125. Widths are set by role as tokens: --w-title 70% for h1, the masthead titles, sign-in, 404 and the greeting's question, and for the date tiles' day numerals as display figures. --w-head 80% for every h2-level head: the rail legends, panel heads, summary heads and the month head. 100% for body, rows, cards, nav, buttons, fields and settings card titles. --w-label 115% for the tiny caps labels. The rule is that the larger the type, the narrower it is set, and the smallest is set wide. This is the optical-size logic, turned into three visible steps.

I chose narrow titles over wide ones. Condensed Archivo and Instrument Sans heads were rewarded in rounds 9, 10 and 11, and condensed type fits the parent's rail legends. I then used the other end of the same axis for the labels, so width carries the whole hierarchy and not just the titles.

Tuning for the new face: condensed titles are set larger to keep their mass. Masthead h1 goes from 2.6rem to clamp(2.35rem,4.9vw,3rem) at weight 640, tracking -.006em (from -.022em, since condensed type crowds when tracked tight) and line-height 1. The question goes to clamp(1.55rem,3vw,1.95rem) at 660. Heads go from 1.15rem to 1.3rem at 620 with tracking 0, and to 1.2rem on the phone. Body gets +.004em letter-spacing and +.04em word-spacing, because Archivo's spaces are narrow for light-on-dark text. font-synthesis is set to none.

MINOR ROLL, capitals limited to one role: the tiny label role (eyebrows, h3, month weekday heads, table captions and column heads, the rail counts, OCT/THU on the date tiles, the settings "changed" badge, the "OK" badge and the "now" lamp legend) is one drawing: Archivo 600 at .72rem, 115% wide, +.06em, uppercase, with the 'case' feature. It keeps each label's own colour.

Carried through, capitals were taken off everything that is not a label. The timetable stamps now read 'was due / 2 days ago' and '27 Sep / 19:56' in lowercase Plex Mono, in the same voice as the facts column. On the glass, '[TODAY]' and '[18 MIN NW]' now read '[today]' and '[18 min NW]', because they are data. 'Ready.' and '?Not found' are sentence case because they are messages. The tube's own labels (NEXT UP, ON THE RADAR, SPENT TODAY, ABOUT, the 404's RANGE and CONTACTS) stay capitals at +.06em, down from .08em.
I put the Status tables' column heads ('what for', 'calls', 'US$') into the label role. They were a lowercase mix of sans and mono, and a column head is the textbook tiny label.

MINOR ROLL, the zero: Plex Mono's default zero is dotted, and its 'zero' feature gives a slashed zero. VT323's default zero is a plain oval that can be read as O, and it too has a slashed 'zero'. designs.name: Long Persistence, Metered
designs.tagline: Long Persistence with its measures drawn as instruments: today's spend swings a phosphor needle on the tube, the month's cost turns printed registers and meters on Status and Settings, and one engraved scale rule divides the parts of every page.
designs.concept: This is Long Persistence with only its pictures changed. The parent's idea, "the phosphor draws, the page prints", now covers the page's measures too. What is live, today's spend, is a moving-coil panel meter drawn in phosphor on the one tube, and its needle kicks and settles as the tube comes on. What is past is printed as flat instruments in bone ink on graphite: a counting register, edgewise meters and split bars. So Status reads as an instrument panel, while the green light stays on the one live dial. One engraved rule runs between the parts of every page: a heavy lead as wide as the icon column, then a hairline ending in a small stop, drawn like the start of a meter's scale.
designs.companions: No new colours. The parent's companions (steel, bone, graphite, sage) keep their jobs. The new drawings use only colours the page already has. Exact #6dff9c (as --phosphor) draws the lit tube dial: scale, ticks, the hatched zone past the limit, and the needle with a hot #e4fff0 core, a halo and a ghost trail showing how far it rose. The printed instruments sit on graphite faces (surface #14191c in a recessed #101417 window) with steel #a8b2bc ticks, a bone #ece6d8 pointer and register digits, and engraved caps legends in the label colour. In the split bars, sent tokens are steel-grey #6f7c86, cached tokens and finished lookups are the lit sage #86d9a6 (the parent's colour for meters and "good"), tokens back are bone #cfc8b9, and a failed lookup is amber (its "needs a look" job). The rules are a pewter lead (#56616a) with a line-2 hairline.
decisions: MAJOR, the instrument panel on Status. The top of Status is now a panel. The one tube (widened from 17.5rem to 21rem, which is the only layout change, made so the dial has room) draws today's spend as a VU-style moving-coil meter in full phosphor. Its scale runs from $0 to 125% of the limit, with major marks at quarters of the limit, and the stretch past the limit is hatched. The pivot sits below the glass, as on a real panel meter. As the tube switches on, the needle kicks up about 17 degrees and settles within 1.45s (none under reduced motion). The figures stay on the glass above the scale.

The past is printed, the present is lit. That keeps the parent's rule that light is only for what is live. Under the masthead, three printed instruments fill what was empty black beside the tube. (1) A counting register: number wheels for the last 30 days' dollars (001.26, with the cents on lighter wheels) and for the model calls (0006). (2) An edgewise meter for the share of input served from the cache, 0-100%. (3) A split bar of the month's tokens (in / cache / out) with a tabular key. Each has an engraved legend. They are aria-hidden pictures of figures the page already writes out under 'What it has cost'. The lamp tables are pushed down about 45px and still end above the fold.

The same drawings carry below the fold and onto other pages. On Status: each kind of call gets a cost-share bar in its US$ cell, each model gets a stacked token bar under its name (the key is the Tokens instrument's), and Waiting gets a split bar of lookups (looked up / waiting / failed) with matching swatches on its tags. On the Settings index, the Spending row gets an edgewise meter on the same 0-125% scale as the tube, with the limit marked by an index triangle and the stretch past it hatched. The Settings > Spending page shows the same meter in its notice (copied settings/spending.html).

I chose not to draw the three lamp groups (Who answers, Keys, Connected to) as dials. A gauge of 'how many are on' would mislead: one key of four is not a fault. It would also repeat the rows under it, and the panel faulted Flight Console's annunciator for that. The dials go on the real quantities (spend, cost, cache, tokens, lookups) and the lamps stay lamps.

MINOR, the drawn divider. I tried five marks in a mock: a trigger flag, a diamond, a down-pointer over a lead, a tiny dial, and a graduated scale. The flag and the pointers read as disclosure carets at 100%. The tiny dial read as a 'spending' icon on every page. The ticks repeat round 7's perforated-edge fault. What I kept is the nearest version that does not hurt the page: a 3px pewter lead, 2.75rem long so it stands over the section icons, a line-2 hairline to the far edge, and a 9px end stop, like the start and end of a meter's scale.

Where the rule goes. It replaces the masthead's plain border on every page (drawn inside the page_head macro, so Plans month, General, Chat and all the others get it). It also sits between parts: on Home over the deck and between its two rows (spanning both columns), on Ideas and To do between the bench and the list, on Plans between the bench and Coming up and before Recently, on Status before the lamps and before each later part, and as the foot's top edge. Status's parts have no box in the parent, so the rule gives them the structure they lacked.

The spacing moves only where a rule needs room. Home is 65px longer. On Ideas and To do the gap is tightened (a 1.75rem rule over a 0.75rem gap), so the list starts where it did. On Status, --shadow and the tube's glow are untouched, screenGlow stays 1.0 and the dial uses the parent's .trace blur and drop-shadow, so it blooms like the other scopes.

In forced colours the rule becomes a CanvasText hairline and the printed gauges are hidden, since their figures are written out elsewhere. Under more contrast the dial loses its blur with the parent's other traces. The words on the page do not change from the parent's: the diff against the parent is 0, and the 7.4% against today on Home is the parent's.

That miss is the words-versus-today measure, 7.4% on Home, and it is inherited: my words match the parent's exactly. ink_on_bg 12.51, brand_on_bg 15.18, brand and screen exact #6dff9c (neon vs today 1.0). Green share of colour: Home 67.2%, Ideas 69.6%, Chat 75.2%, Status 58.7%. Hue entropy: Home .492, Ideas .382, Chat .368, Status .378. Bright green on Status is 0.80 per mille, up from the parent's 0.39, because of the lit dial. Kinds dE 13.6 typical / 5.5 deuteranopia / 7.4 protanopia; sections 13.6 / 5.5 / 5.4. Greeting corner pixel (1150,120) = (26,36,47), the parent's unchanged. No sideways scroll on any rendered page. Smallest text 12px (11.97 on General, as in the parent). 0 targets under 44px. Home 1699px tall, against the parent's 1634. The variant lint passes and removed.txt is empty.
strengths: Status now looks like an instrument panel at a glance, above the fold. It has a lit moving-coil meter for today, and a printed register, meter and split bar for the month, all drawing real figures (the spend, 30-day cost and calls, cache share, token split). None of it is costume.

It extends the parent's idea instead of fighting it. Light stays on the one live instrument, and the full phosphor effect (bloom, blur, scanlines, halo on the needle, needle afterglow, power-on kick) goes where attention belongs. The past is printed, matte.

One drawing language runs through it. The tube dial, the edgewise meters on Status, the Settings row and the Spending page share one scale (0 to 125% of the limit, hatched past the limit). The index triangle marks the limit wherever there is one, and the page rules are drawn like the start and end of that scale.

The rule is one device on every page (every masthead, section breaks on Home, Status, Ideas, To do and Plans, and the foot). It gives Status's unboxed parts structure and gives the deck's two rows a clear break. Its lead aligns over the section icons.

The cost tables below the fold gain bar charts (cost share per kind, token split per model, lookup progress) whose colours share one key. The Settings index and the Spending page carry the same cost meter, so the readout reaches every page that shows a cost.
Nothing else moves. Colours, type, words, targets and contrast are the parent's, so the judges can see what the graphics alone do.
weaknesses: The demo spends $0.00 today and 0% comes from the cache, so both needles rest at zero in the stills. The lit dial reads as a meter at rest, not a reading, and the power-on kick happens before the harness takes its shot.

The rolled change asked for Status to be drawn as instruments, but the three lamp tables (the 'is it working' half of Status) are unchanged. I judged dials over on/off counts misleading and repetitive, but a judge may find that half of the roll unanswered.

The divider is modest: a pewter lead, a hairline and a stop. It is a thick-then-thin rule with an end mark, not a pictorial ornament. It is quiet at 100%, and Home, Chat and Ideas differ from the parent by little more than it.
The register's number wheels and the recessed gauge windows lean slightly skeuomorphic beside the parent's flat legend tables. The small calls register sits a little apart from its 'CALLS' label.
The tube is 3.5rem wider and the printed strip pushes Status's lamp tables down about 45px. Home is 65px longer because of the two rules.
The Settings row meter reads today's spend back out of the row's own sentence ('About $X spent today.'), because the index view passes no number. That is fragile if the wording changes.
Every gauge is aria-hidden, so a screen reader relies on the figures written elsewhere (the words under 'What it has cost' and the row sentences), which all exist.

designs.name: Slate Flight Console
designs.tagline: Flight Console's bays, lamps and flight-plan drawings rebuilt in Evening Listing's materials: slate for what the family keeps, steel pencil for the plan and for "here", green-black glass for what the machine says, and the phosphor lit only on what is live.
designs.concept: A calm night shift at a 1969 flight console, built from the evening listing's materials. You read how things stand from the lamps and the readouts. Slate carries what the family keeps and presses, in visible steps, with every list banded the way the listing's rows are. Steel pencil draws the flight plan and latches "here" and "today". Her words sit on green-black glass. #6dff9c lights only what is live: the mark, "mind", Send, focus, the NOW needle, working lamps and the tubes. Amber is painted, never lit, and means one thing: "needs a look".
designs.companions: 1) Slate, from Evening Listing, in four steps a glance can tell apart: plotting board #10161a (the tile columns, track board, Status panel, Settings nav); bay #151b1e; banded row #1a2125 (every other row in every list: Coming up, To do, the setup holds, the kids, the attention list, data tables, people, memory); keys #1f272e. On the board a row bands at #161d22 (the Settings nav and the To do crew board). The bar is #0f1417. 2) Steel pencil: #84a0c4 for lines and pictograms, #58697a secondary, and #3a454c for every divider inside a bay (the tile | body and figure | body lines, the Status grid, the rail's leaders). Labels are #a4b0c2: captions, legends, tallies, the "in 2 days" in Coming up, and the T-minus labels. 3) Steel reverse video (#71899c with a #a9c4d8 cap and dark ink) marks "here": the bar key, the All ideas/Month tabs, the Settings nav and the menu. It also marks "today" on the month's today cell and the month-track lamp. Her dateline beside her name ("Vera | TUE 29 SEP") is set in #a9c4d8 steel. 4) Denim #9db6d6, underlined and in sentence case, is every link: All plans, Add an idea, All 4, Change a key, Setup, and now the way back ("Settings ›", "Ideas ›"). 5) Kind colours sit in tinted icon wells on idea cards: color-mix(kind 14%, #1a2125) for the cool kinds (trip, day trip, outing, show, event) and 6% for restaurant, activity and seasonal, with the icon in the kind colour. The Ideas page has 44px wells top right; Home's Lately added has 32px wells beside the kind name. 6) Cobalt #4f60e6 at washGlow 2.4 is the second light in the top right of her glass (samples (25,32,45)). 7) Amber #ffb850 is matte and has one job, "needs a look": the setup bay's 2px #7a5d31 top edge, its head and three painted hold lamps, the Late and Holds figures on the rail, "2 late" and "was due" words, late To do cards' inset edge, and caution windows on Status.
decisions: STRUCTURE (Flight Console) kept whole: the clean sheet and 15 templates, bays led by a figure or a 76px tile column, the four-week track with numbered stops, the month track, T-minus holds, punched idea cards, the Capcom transcript with its loop tile, console plates, keys with lamps, IBM Plex Sans/Condensed/Mono with VT323 on the tubes only.

COLOUR (Evening Listing, Relit) now shows as material, not as a 2-4 RGB shift. Every list in a bay is banded: every other row is #1a2125 on the #151b1e bay, with no rule between rows. The fill hangs 12px outside the words so the text lines up with the head. Inside bays, dividers are steel pencil #3a454c. Kind-tinted icon wells replace the steel pictograms. The To do and Coming up heads carry a tally in the listing's head-column grammar ('4 open · 2 late', '4 more · next in 2 days'). I used #1a2125 for the bands, not the critic's #161d22, because #161d22 on a #151b1e bay is 1-4 RGB and invisible. #161d22 bands only on the darker plotting board.

THE RAIL becomes the console's foot and a row of links. It now follows the words and the tube in the DOM, so the ask box is still the first stop after the bar and the rail's keys come after the tube's link. Each readout-cell is a 52px <a>: Plans goes to /plans, To do to /tasks, Late to /tasks?status=open, Ideas to /ideas, Holds to /setup. Each is read along a dotted steel leader to its Plex Mono figure, the listing's row-to-facts grammar. The TODAY slab is gone. The date is now her dateline beside her name, so nothing repeats 'here' under the steel Home key, and the phone's 700px steel band is gone.

STATUS: the annunciator is the list. Three groups (Who answers, Keys, Connected to) sit in rows. Each row has a 12.5rem slate legend cell set into the panel's steel grid and a grid of windows on the plotting board. Each window has a lamp bar, a tracked-caps legend and a second line in words: 'set in the environment', 'not configured', the model's name. The model-switch form now lives inside its window, so nothing was removed. A working window is green-black glass #0f1a13 with the lamp bar at full #6dff9c and its legend in --lit #86d9a6 with a 0 0 .45em halo. An off window is matte slate with a hollow ring. A caution window is slate with an amber top edge. 'Change a key' is a denim link under the Keys legend. The three repeated lists are gone. The key underneath is the one FIG caption left on Status.

AMBER IS MATTE. .lamp.amber and .section-card.look::after are solid #ffb850 with a #b9843a rim, a 1px #ffe2b3 inset cap and at most 0 0 2px. The text-shadow is gone from the Late/Holds figures and from .hold-t. .light.part lost its bloom. Caution annunciators lost their amber fill and glow. The T-minus labels, in the tile and in the list, are sequence labels, so they moved from amber to steel label. That leaves the setup bay's amber as the edge, the head and three painted lamps.

HOME CREW BOARD folded into the To do head ('4 open · 2 late', the late part in amber words). The To do bay became a slim bay with a pictogram tile, matching Lately added. The full board and legend stay on the To do page, where its rows are now banded on the board.

CHAT split, desktop and phone: .said-them uses minmax(0,1fr) 34px (28px on the phone). The family's square slate bubbles with their steel cap stand at the right beside their steel-ringed key. Vera's rounded glass hangs from the loop rail at the left, 12% short of the far side. .said-text is capped at 62ch, so material and side both say who spoke.

HOME ORDER AND FIGURES: the kids' wishes left the top, which lifts the track and Coming up by about 185px and removes the dead tile column. The kids sit side by side in banded cells. .agenda .when is Plex Mono, tabular with a slashed zero, split into two timetable lines: the day, then the hour in heading ink with 'in 2 days' in steel label. Before the split, 'Thursday 1 October, 10:00' wrapped at the comma in a 200px cell. The first stop on the track is placed at least 0.95 day (about 33px) after the NOW needle, so it no longer sits on it.

PLANS: month rows 64px, the track's FIG caption dropped, and the track board's padding trimmed, so the whole month and today's steel cell fit in one 900px screen. table.month th and table.data th rose to .75rem, so the whole app now has a 12px floor.

The edge is an inset shadow, the lit state a drop-shadow of the well alone, and the focus ring sits at outline-offset -10px. The ask bar's select and mic, the dictation mics, card-title links (padding-block 10px, taken back with a negative margin), crumbs, event links, 'All' links, fold summaries and phone tool icons were all brought to 44px. Result: 0 targets under 44px on Home (62), To do (98), Ideas (50), Chat, Status, Plans, the form and General, down from 4, 19, 13, 3, 3, 3, 8 and 3.

The new-idea form's 290px drawing of itself is gone and the form now takes the whole bay behind a slim idea tile. Crumbs are sentence-case denim with a steel ›. Tracking on 12px caps went from .12-.16em to .06-.08em (eyebrow, labels, kind names, speakers, rail, board, legends, table heads, and the plate at .1em). .hold-lamp i went from 11px to 12px. Page heads are 20px tighter on every page.

designs.concept: FamilyDB is set as the family's own photocopied zine. The family's things are scraps of grained black card, each torn along an edge and held down by one strip of masking tape. Titles are cut-out letters on a torn masthead strip in the part's colour, section heads are punched label tape, and red marker circles where you are, today, what is late and what needs a look. The machine is the only thing printed in glow ink: the mark, the primary sticker, the word MIND, focus, the lamps and Vera's own name. Wherever the machine is live, the card is torn open and the green tube glows up through the hole, with bloom, scanlines, sweep and afterglow. It should feel handmade, warm and a bit playful, with every word at one 17px size and the light only where attention belongs.
designs.companions: Red marker #dc747d (`accent` and ring.svg/scrawl.svg; darker #8f454d as a ransom paper) is kept to four jobs: the loop round where you are (bar, phone tab bar, settings nav), today's leaf and today's month cell, the scrawl under a late date, and 'Needs a look' and the setup steps. Kraft #a3865f is the calendar leaves and cut-out letters. Newsprint #cdc8b8 is cut-out letters and plain headline strips. Graphite #3a3f3a with a light edge is the third ransom paper. Masking-tape beige (`secondary` #cbbf9c) makes the tape on every scrap, the ways to start, the quiet keys, the fold chevrons and the tips bullets. Brown card (#29251f bubble-them, #231f19) holds the family's chat lines, the setup note, Save a thought and Something to eat. The section colours, lowered in chroma, become dark label tape, stamped title icons, kind dot stickers and tinted masthead strips: Ideas lilac, Plans slate blue, To do olive, Wishes pink, Family amber. Home, Vera, Status, Settings and sign-in have no colour of their own, so they get black Dymo tape (#6b716c mixed dark, embossed white letters) and no longer get red. Grown-ups have amber avatar stickers and kids pink.
decisions: One type size for everything: html at 106.25% (17px) and `body * { font-size: 1em }`. Rank comes from face, weight, width, case, colour and space. There are eight roles, all at 17px. TITLE is cut-out letters on a torn masthead. HEAD is label tape in Archivo 700 caps, tracked .1em. SUB is Space Mono 700 caps with a dashed cut line. ITEM is Bricolage 700 and TEXT is Bricolage 400. TYPED is Space Mono for labels, dates, who/when and table heads. NOTE is Victor Mono italic for 'in 2 days', 'was due', optional, changed and the motto. KEY is Archivo 800 caps. TUBE is Workbench, with Sixtyfour for the one big figure on each screen.

Cut-out titles (the `ransom()` macro) now read as words. The pieces butt together (`margin: 0 -0.03em`) and word gaps are 0.62em, or 0.95em in a page title. Each word is cut from one paper in turn: newsprint, then graphite #3a3f3a with an inset light edge, then kraft. Each word has at most two odd pieces, at fixed places. There are three cuts: Archivo 900 wide, Fraunces soft 900, and Space Mono bold. No cut reads a size smaller, and no piece leans more than 2 degrees. The words stay in `.sr` text and the letters stay aria-hidden.

The page title outranks the section heads because of its room and paper. `.page-title` (title row, stamp and lede) is one torn masthead strip at least min(100%, 36rem) wide, in its part's colour, taped at a corner. The h2 tape is toned down to Archivo 700, 100% width, .1em tracking.

There is now a third level. h3 and table captions are typed capitals in the label colour with a dashed cut line running to the edge. The caption keeps table layout, using an inline line clipped by overflow.

Folds follow one rule. A panel-level fold wears the h2 label tape: `.h2` now carries the full tape rule, and Ideas' 'Save a thought for later' is wrapped in `.h2` (words unchanged). A fold inside a card stays Bricolage 700 in sentence case. Summaries use `text-wrap: balance`.

Tubes are set in Workbench (BLED 20). Next up now fits in about 3 lines and the Ideas radar in 3. Sixtyfour is kept for .next-title, .on-radar-count, .readout-figure and the 404's '404'. The phosphor blur is only on text lines. The reverse labels (NEXT UP, ON THE RADAR) sit at z-index 5 above the scanlines, crisp, with their own 14px halo. The Ideas tube is shorter and its spill is cut to 16px + 36px.

Tears are tiles of a fixed size, not % polygons: tear-top/bottom 173x6 and left/right 6x131, applied with `mask` and `repeat-x`/`repeat-y`. Tube holes use 211x10 and 10x157 tiles, made by `_work/tears.py`. The grain of a tear is the same on any width. `--tear-x`/`--tear-y` offsets make neighbours tear differently.

Scraps in a grid lie true (`--tilt: 0`: panels, cards, idea cards, settings cards, status monitors). Only loose scraps lean: the ask card, the setup note, Save a thought, title strips, leaves, tape, bubbles, events. Card tape varies on primes: `5n+2` is the other corner, `7n+2`/`7n+4` go straight across, and `5n+3`/`7n+6` are glued down with no tape, about a third. So the tapes never line up in columns.

Glow ink is kept to the live things, and 'VERA' now joins them. Her name, above her chat lines and beside her screen on Home, is printed in brand with the kit's three-layer halo. MIND is dark card printed in green, and its word has a 7px green halo spilling past the cut pieces. The mark, cursor, SEND/ADD stickers, focus, lamps (breathing), meters, ticks and the card hover afterglow (1.2s) stay as they were.

Home is rebuilt from its content. The question, box and her line are on the left, with the kids' wishes pinned under them. The card torn open over Next up is on the right, with the setup note taped on underneath. Coming up and To do sit side by side, then Lately added. The kraft leaves deliberately hang off the torn edge of the card (`margin-left: -2.1rem`, wide screens only). On a leaf, month and weekday are at .6 opacity with no dark band, so the wide black day leads.

Where no page colour applies, Dymo tape replaces red, and off lamps are pencil rings (`--dim`), no longer red. Fold chevrons are tape beige, `ol.steps` numbers are ink-2, and tips bullets are beige. The red marker loop is sized to its words: settings-nav links are `width: fit-content`, and the phone tab bar has .5rem side padding with an 86% x 92% loop.

Typesetting. Figures are `tabular-nums lining-nums` on .when, .meta, event times, month days, who/when, counts and the leaves. A running em/i is Bricolage 600 upright, and the pen hand stays for the pen notes. The measure is 64ch on .lede, .hint, .help, panel paragraphs, `main > p` and .lead. Leading is 1.6 for body text and about 1.35 inside tapes, leaves and captions.

Controls. Fields are cut into the card with an inset and a green caret. Textareas are ruled notebook pages. Selects use `appearance: base-select` with a card picker, a glowing tick and `position-try-order: normal`, so the list drops below its box. Checkboxes are pen squares that fill with glow ink. The tick is now a 44px button drawn as a 28px pen box inside it. Bar tools, section links and the phone tools are 2.75rem targets. Save is a torn strip pinned along the foot.

Guidelines bent: STYLE.md's type scale is gone (one size). The top afterglow is only a breath under an opaque masthead. The greeting glow (E7) is replaced by the tube's spill through the torn card. Nothing was removed: removed.txt is empty, and every form keeps its csrf and once tokens. Words are 3.7% changed at most (Home, the hidden title text).
designs.measures: Full render: 0 hard checks failed, 0 guidelines missed. ink_on_bg 14.46:1, brand_on_bg 15.08:1, brand_neon_vs_today 1.0. Green share of colour and hue entropy: Home 47.8% / 0.524; Ideas 91.2% / 0.243; Chat 64.7% / 0.369 (up from 46.8 because VERA is now in glow ink); Status 55.2% / 0.437. Bright green permille: Home 3.67, Ideas 11.89, Chat 1.44, Status 1.34. CIEDE2000 kinds typ/deu/pro 15.4 / 8.0 / 10.4; sections 14.2 / 8.0 / 10.7 (tritan 5.5 both). Greeting pixels: (1150,120) = (23,32,26), the grained ground above Next up's torn hole. (100,640) = (69,68,58), now the tape of a 'ways to start' strip, since the greeting glow is replaced by the tube's spill. Smallest words 17px on every page; no sideways scroll on any page (the 5px overflow on chat-phone mid-iteration was fixed). Words changed at most 3.7% (Home). Click targets under 44px: Home 56 -> 11, Home phone 57 -> 12, To do 21, Ideas 17, Form 10, the rest 2-7.
strengths: Each material has one job, and those jobs hold on every page (Plans list, Month, To do, Family, Wishes, Settings, General, Status, an idea's page, sign-in and 404), so it reads as a system rather than a one-off effect.

The cut-out titles now read at a glance: pieces are glued edge to edge, each word is one paper with at most two odd pieces, and every letter has visible paper. Each page title sits on a torn masthead that carries its lede and clearly outranks the label tape below it.
There are three visible heading levels without a second type size: masthead strip, then label tape, then typed capitals with a cut line. Fold summaries follow one rule.

The phosphor comes back where the machine is. The card is torn open over Next up, the Ideas radar, READY, the 404 and the spend readout, with bloom, scanlines, sheen, sweep, blips, power-on and afterglow. Workbench halves the tube width, so Next up fits in 3 lines, and the reverse labels sit crisp above the glass.
Glow ink is kept to the live things, which now include Vera's own name: the machine's voice is lit while her bubbles stay matte card.
Tears have the same grain at any width, and grid scraps lie true with tape on prime cycles and a third glued down, so the handmade look no longer turns mechanical.
Red marker has its four jobs back. Status and Settings are calm, with Dymo tape and pencil-ring off lamps, so 'Needs a look', the late scrawls, today's ring and the where-you-are loop stand out.
Typesetting: tabular lining figures in dates and times, a 64ch measure on help and ledes, upright Bricolage for running emphasis, and kraft leaves led by the day number.
Accessibility is better: 17px minimum everywhere, the tick is a 44px button, Home's small targets dropped from 23 to 11, and focus is a clean 2px brand ring.
weaknesses: Ideas is still about 91% green in its colour share on the first screen. The radar tube is shorter and its spill smaller, but it is the only saturated thing on a page of dark card.

The one-size rule means a page title never gets bigger. The masthead strip gives it room and weight, but on dense pages (General, Status) the eye can still land on the green SAVE sticker or a lit tube before the title.

Cut-out titles cost more width than set type. 'Things to do' and 'Sign in to FamilyDB' wrap to two lines on a phone, and a long title from a template (an idea's name) falls back to one newsprint strip, which is consistent but plainer.
Ideas (17 small targets) and To do (21) still have many targets under 44px: the filter labels' fields, kind stickers and the 'Edit, complete, or snooze' rows.
Grain SVGs, tiled tear masks and drop-shadow filters on every scrap make the page heavier to paint than a flat sheet. That is fine on a laptop, but on an old phone it may cost scrolling smoothness.
The Settings index cards still share one paper and one stamp style, so beyond the lead card's tape variety, nine cards read as a regular grid. That is right for a grid, but less zine-like.

Workbench at BLED 20 is legible but has a pixel edge. At 17px, the dim lines on the tubes ('North at the top...', 'OF THE $2.00 DAILY LIMIT') are the hardest words on the page to read, though they pass 5.8:1.

crit: 1. Make the cut-out titles read at a glance. This is the signature, and today it is the thing that reads worst (`.ransom`, the `ransom()` macro; worst on Home's 'What's on your mind?', 'Things to do' and 'Settings'). Letters are spaced out by `.ransom .l { margin: .1em .045em; padding: .2em .3em }`. Some tiles have no paper, or near-black paper: `7n+4` is transparent, `7n+2` is #2a2f2b and `7n+5` is #1f2320, and on the #1c201d ask card they vanish, so 'WHAT'S' reads as W H A T. Fixes: set the letter margin to `0 -0.03em` so the pieces touch like glued cut-outs, and widen the `.ransom .w` gap to 0.9em (1.2em in `.page-head h1`) so a word gap is clearly bigger than a letter gap. Give every letter a visible paper: swap the two near-blacks for a light-edged graphite, #3a3f3a with `box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgb(255 255 255/.08)`. Drop the letters that look a size smaller, which breaks the one-size rule itself: `7n+6` at `font-stretch: 62%` and the Fraunces italic 800 on `7n+5`. Keep three cuts (Archivo 900 wide, Fraunces soft roman, Space Mono bold), put at most two odd papers in a word with the rest on one paper, and keep rotation to 2deg or less.

2. Set the tubes in Workbench, not Sixtyfour; it keeps the one-size rule and halves the width. Measured from the font files: Sixtyfour's advance is 1.0em and Workbench's 0.5em, and both have x-height 0.625 and cap height 0.875. VT323's x-height is 0.40, so it would read a size smaller. Use `.crt-tube { font-family: "Workbench", var(--terminal); font-variation-settings: "BLED" 20, "SCAN" 0 }`, and keep Sixtyfour only for `.next-title`, `.on-radar-count` and `.readout-figure`. Next up goes from 6 lines to about 3, and the Ideas radar from 5 lines to about 3 (11 to about 6 on the phone), which also eases Ideas' 92% green first screen. On Ideas, also cut the outer bloom from 70px to about 40px so it stops washing over the filter card. Then fix the soft reverse labels (NEXT UP reads 'MEXT UP'). `.crt-tube > :not(.radar) { filter: blur(.35px) }` blurs `.next-label` and `.on-radar-label`, and the scanlines in `.crt-tube::before` (z-index 3, 0.4 alpha) cut across their dark letters. Move the blur onto the other lines only (`.crt-tube p:not(.next-label):not(.on-radar-label)`), and give the labels `position: relative; z-index: 5` with their own `box-shadow: 0 0 14px` halo, so they sit crisp on top of the glass.

3. Rank without size on the text-heavy pages. (a) The page title must outrank its section heads. On Status, General and To do, the wide Archivo 800 capitals of the h2 tape ('WHO ANSWERS', 'WHERE HOME IS', 'ADD SOMETHING TO DO') shout louder than the small cut-out title strip. Draw the torn strip on `.page-title`, which holds the title row and the lede, instead of `.title-row::before`, so the lede is typed onto a masthead at least `min(100%, 36rem)` wide. Tone the h2 down to `font-weight: 700; font-stretch: 100%; letter-spacing: .1em`. (b) Add the missing third level. `h3` ('By kind of call', 'By model', 'Next to be looked up', 'Calls that ended oddly') is Bricolage 700, the same as the items under it. Set it as typed capitals with a cut line: `font-family: var(--type); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em; color: var(--label); display: flex; gap: .6em`, plus `h3::after { content: ''; flex: 1; border-top: 1.5px dashed var(--line-2) }`. (c) One rule for folds. A fold at panel level (the `summary > .h2` in 'Add something to do', `details.fold > summary` in 'Exact position and travel times' and 'The server's log', Ideas' 'Save a thought for later') wears the h2 label tape: give `.h2` the h2 rule. A fold inside a card ('Edit, complete, or snooze', 'Everything else') stays Bricolage 700 in sentence case. Add `text-wrap: balance` to `summary`, so the phone no longer shows 'ADD SOMETHING TO / DO'.

4. Give the red marker back its four jobs: where you are, today, late, and needs a look. `.in-home, .in-chat, .in-status, .in-settings, .in-none { --sec: var(--accent) }` makes every h2 on Status and the Settings pages red-brown tape ('Models and prices', 'Recent activity', 'Waiting', 'Where home is', 'This page'), and tints the Vera, Status, Settings and General title strips red. Red also draws every fold chevron (`details:not(.menu) > summary::before`), the `ol.steps` numbers and the `ul.tips` bullets. On Status, `.light.off` is drawn in `--danger`, and those 7 of 13 lamps read as the same red circles. For the parts with no colour of their own, use classic black Dymo tape (`--sec: #3b3f3a`, embossed white letters). Draw the chevrons and list numbers in `var(--ink-2)` or tape beige `var(--secondary)`, and draw an off lamp as a pencil ring (`.light.off { border-color: var(--dim) }`). Also size the loop to the words: `ring.svg` is stretched `100% 100%` over the whole link. It flattens to a 240px ellipse round 'General' in `.settings-nav`, and on the phone tab bar (`.places a[aria-current]`, `92% 100%`) it overruns its cell, touching the screen edge at about 8px on Home. Use `width: fit-content` on the settings links, give the tab bar `padding-inline: .5rem`, and set the phone loop to about `86% 92%`.

5. Fix what is broken. (a) `ul.plain, ol.plain { padding: 0 }` (specificity 0,1,1) beats `.agenda` and `.checklist { padding: .6rem 1.4rem .8rem }` (0,1,0). So Home's To do checkboxes sit flush on the torn left edge of the card and the dashed row rules run edge to edge. Write `.panel.agenda, .panel.checklist { padding: .6rem 1.4rem .8rem }`. If the kraft leaves should hang off the card, make it deliberate: `.agenda .chip { margin-left: -2.1rem }`. (b) On the 404, the centred '404' (`.lost .radar-say`, tracked .25em) lands on the radar's '1w' ring label. Move it below the centre, or hide the ring labels on the 404 radar.

6. Stop the handmade look turning mechanical in the strict grids. `.section-card` (all 9 Settings cards) has one tape position (`--tape-x: 1.5rem; --tape-r: -36deg`), and `.card:nth-child(3n…)` and `.idea-card:nth-child(2n)` repeat with the grid's own period, so the tapes line up in columns. Cycle on primes (`:nth-child(5n+2)`, `7n+4`), leave about one scrap in three with no tape (glued down), and set `--tilt: 0` on cards in grids (Settings, Ideas, To do, Status) so the grid lines stay true. Let only the loose scraps tilt: the ask card, the setup note, the title strips, the leaves, the tape. The tears are % polygons (`--tear-*`, about 35 points across), so on a 1200px panel they stretch into an even sawtooth about 35px apart. Tile a tear of fixed size instead: `mask: url(tear.svg) top left / 173px 6px repeat-x, linear-gradient(#000 0 0) 0 5px / 100% 100% no-repeat`. Then the tear has the same grain at any width.

7. Print the machine's voice in glow ink, and tidy the phone chat. Her lines are plain black card, and her name (`.thread > li:not(.said-them) .said-by strong`, and `.speaker strong` beside her screen on Home) is set in ink. Print 'VERA' in glow ink with the kit's layered halo: `color: var(--brand); text-shadow: 0 0 1px rgb(109 255 156/.8), 0 0 8px rgb(109 255 156/.45), 0 0 20px rgb(109 255 156/.2)`. That puts light where attention belongs without greening her bubbles. On the phone (below 30rem), the avatar column leaves an empty strip about 60px wide beside her 6-line bubble, and her text runs only about 26 characters to a line. Put the sticker or screen inline in `.said-by`, and indent the family's bubbles 2.5rem instead: the left and right shape stays and the measure grows. Make the bar's tool icons (`.tools > a`, `.menu > summary`) 2.75rem squares: 23 of Home's 56 click targets are under 44px.

8. Typesetting details. (a) On the kraft leaves, the day number, the thing the eye wants, loses to 'OCT': dim `.chip-mon` and `.chip-dow` to `opacity: .6` and drop the 12% black band behind the month (the `linear-gradient` 0 to 1.35rem in `.chip`), so the Archivo 900 wide `.chip-day` leads. (b) Line the figures up: add `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums` on `.when`, `.meta`, `.event time` and `table.month time`, so times such as 10:00, 13:00 and 09:00 stack. (c) `em, i { font-family: var(--hand) }` turns emphasis inside help text into handwriting, as with the 'A record' on General. Keep the pen hand for `.rel, .optional, .changed, .reminder, .did, .warn`, and set a running `em` as Bricolage 600 upright. (d) Set a measure: General's help and To do's lede run 95 to 105 characters; add `.lede, .hint, .help, .panel > p { max-width: 64ch }`, and keep the 1.6 leading for body text only, with 1.35 inside the tapes and leaves.

firstDraft.name: Glow Ink Zine
firstDraft.concept: FamilyDB as the family's own photocopied zine. Scraps of grained black card are torn along an edge and held down by one strip of masking tape. Page titles are ransom letters cut from kraft, newsprint, red and black paper. Section heads are punched label tape in each part's colour, and where-you-are, today and late are circled or scrawled in red marker. The machine is the one thing printed in glow ink. Where it is live, the card is torn open over its green tube, and the phosphor glows up through the hole with scanlines, bloom, sweep and afterglow. The feel is handmade, warm and a bit playful, with the light where attention belongs.

designs.name: Ceefax Evening
designs.tagline: The family's planner as a teletext service on a warm CRT: every page numbered, one double-height headline to a page, every section led by a mosaic drawing, and the phosphor lit only where something is live.
designs.concept: Every page of FamilyDB is a page of a teletext service on a CRT, set on a strict 40-column grid. There is a page number in the header row (P100 Home, 150 Vera, 200 Ideas, 300 Plans, 400 To do, 500 Wishes, 600 Memory, 700 Family, 800 Status, 880 Setup, 890 Settings with 891 to 899 below it), one double-height headline to a view, and every section opens with a drawing in separated mosaic blocks. It should feel like a calm evening with the TV on: flat slate blocks in grounded section colours and ochre print from the broadcaster, with the bright phosphor kept for what is live or what you act on.
designs.companions:
Ochre #d2ba96 (the `label` token, a greyer ochre than before) is the broadcaster's print. It is used for page numbers, dates and times that stand alone (a plan's date, a task's due date), small-caps labels, the bracketed [IN 2 DAYS] asides, field labels, who said a line, and the ochre details in the drawings (bulb base, calendar rings, bow). It is never used for body text.
Each part of the site has a grounded, lower-chroma colour. It is used for the part's headline, its drawing, its current key in the bar (in inverse), its page numbers, the mosaic rules under its heads and a deep tinted band behind the page head:
- Ideas: heather #cb86c1
- Plans: sky #93d6ee
- To do: straw #e3d688
- Wishes: rose #eb99ac
- Family, Memory and setup: amber #efaf69
- Home, Vera, Status and Settings: eucalyptus-sage #98d2c2 (the `accent`, now clearly apart from the signature green)
The idea kinds add moss #7db581 (outing) and terracotta #e68867 (seasonal).
Blocks are cool slate #10191d on the green-black ground. Her chat bubbles are forest #131f18 and the family's are umber #241d15. Kids' initials are rose and grown-ups' initials are amber.
The bright #6dff9c appears only on:
- the mark and its cursor
- the one primary key per view
- the lit ask box and the key word "mind"
- focus rings, lamps and ticks (`lit` #7ded9f)
- the monitors and her glyph screen
decisions: A clean sheet (variants/r12-wild-2/sheet.css, about 103 KB) with my own templates: base, _ui, _ask, home, ideas, settings_section, 404, 403, and a generated _pics.html. The sprite is redrawn as 10x10 mosaics. removed.txt is empty, and every form keeps its csrf and once tokens.

Type is snapped to VT323's pixel. It is drawn on a 0.04em pixel, so it is set only at 25px, 50px and 75px. T1 is 75px in double height and is the ONE double-height line of a view: a page's title, or Home's question. T2 is 50px single height in capitals, used for section heads, band heads, block titles and the month. T3 is 25px with one pixel (0.04em) of tracking, used for the bar, keys, buttons, tabs, labels, dates, page numbers and asides. On a phone (two device pixels to one CSS pixel), T1 and T2 are 37.5px. On desktops narrower than 1200px, T1 steps down to 50px. `--page` is 1200px, so `--col` is 30px at 1280.

Two voices. The machine speaks in teletext: VT323 for heads, keys, labels, and any date, time or sum that stands on its own, with tabular figures. The family and Vera are set in print: Atkinson Hyperlegible at 17/1.55. firstDraft.name: Ceefax Evening
firstDraft.concept: Every page of FamilyDB becomes a page of a teletext service, set the way Ceefax set one on a CRT. There are 40 strict columns and a page number on every page (P100 Home, 150 Vera, 200 Ideas, 300 Plans, 400 To do, 500 Wishes, 600 Memory, 700 Family, 800 Status, 890 Settings and its subpages 891 to 899). designs.name: Zenith Desk
designs.tagline: A planetarium's control desk after dark: Vera's thread at the zenith of a charted dome, everything else in orbit round it, lit by green phosphor and read by a red desk lamp.
designs.concept: The page is a planetarium's control desk at night. The ground is a night-teal dome drawn as a star chart, and the conversation with Vera sits at its zenith. On Home the family's plans now rise over her screen as the dome's own stars: the next one pinging green on the meridian, the later ones further out towards the rim, on a 1w/2w/4w scale. On Chat the meridian falls from her screen through the thread. Green phosphor is the machine's light and nothing else. A red desk lamp marks only coordinates. Everything else is printed like an atlas: parchment serif names, maroon for the family's own words, dark chart teal. It should feel quiet, nocturnal and a little wondrous.
designs.companions: Red lamp (label #db99a0, OKLCH 0.75/0.08/12). It now marks only coordinates: date leaves, "in 2 days" pills, said-at times, catalogue numbers (#1 · ACTIVITY), To do's "Due 2026-09-27 19:56" stamp, weekday heads, step numbers, the dome's hour labels and its 1w/2w/4w week scale, and the Greek letters before section names. Desk maroon (bubble-them #301c1f) is the family's material: their chat bubbles, the warm pool in the corner of the desk panels (setup, wishes), and the weekend columns of the month at 42%. Parchment starlight (heading #eee7d9) is every title and heading. Atlas gold (todo at 22%) is the dashed ecliptic. The section and kind colours are star colours: lilac ideas, blue-white plans (also the colour of the plan stars on the dome), straw to-do, K-star amber people, and orchid wishes. Wishes moved from #f2a1c5 to #eea1d3, hue 341, so they sit 13.0 ΔE from the lamp instead of 9.5. Coral seasons and soft-green outing complete the set. They show as a glowing dot in the margin of each catalogue entry and as the star under the current place in the bar.

It is a terminal record, a label column and a value column (NEXT UP | Pho Oregon / when / > 4 more on the radar), with no radar of its own. The west orbit now opens with α Coming up. firstDraft.name: Zenith Desk
firstDraft.concept: The page is a planetarium's control desk after dark. The ground is the dome, a deep night teal charted in faint lines. The conversation with Vera sits at its zenith: on Home it sits at the centre of a real star chart, and on Chat it hangs off a meridian with each line's time plotted like a coordinate. Everything else sits round it like the instruments of the desk. Green phosphor is the machine's light (her screen, the lit box, the button, the monitors, the lamps). A red desk lamp at OKLCH hue 12 is the light people read the chart by: coordinates, dates, times, the rim's scale, and a warm pool where the family's own words sit. It should feel quiet, nocturnal and a little wondrous: bright only where the machine is, and printed like an atlas everywhere else.

designs.name: Single Quote
designs.tagline: A trading terminal that quotes one thing at a time: the thing that matters now, set large, with every other screen a numbered key away.
designs.concept: FamilyDB as a calm trading terminal. Each screen quotes one thing large, the way a quote screen shows one security: a condensed title, its figure in the section's colour, and under the unit a change line saying what moved or what comes next. Under each quote runs a short tape of the next few items, and everything else sits one numbered key away. A command line (FamilyDB > SETTINGS > GENERAL▌) and a function-key legend frame every page. Only live things give off phosphor light, and that light has the original tube's bloom, blur, scanlines and afterglow. The feel is exact and quiet, with a hint of the trading floor: a figure that has just arrived flashes, then settles.
designs.companions: Violet (OKLCH hue 304) has two jobs. As ink #b3a2cb it is the terminal's legend: every small monospaced capital, including key numbers, the command path, crumbs, tile legends, field legends on every form (now a rule, not one form's style), column heads, ids and who spoke in the tape. As a faint tint it runs through everything solid: surfaces #18161c, #1f1d24 and #28242c, the keycaps and the monitor bezel #232027. The result is a plum-graphite housing on a green-black ground. Bone ink #eae6dd (headings #f0ece4) carries the words. Calm sage #91dbab is the lit/accent colour: ticks, done, OK, the box being typed in, Vera's name in the tape, and link underlines on Home, Vera, Status and Settings. The section colours are muted: ideas #ab94e7, plans #7dcae5, todo #e1c570, people/today #ec9d53, shows #e99dbe, seasons #dc7863, outing #86db9d. Each appears only as that section's figure, a kind label, a date (the Coming-up tape's stamps are plans-cyan) or the change arrow. Amber also marks late and 'needs a look'. Red appears only for a real fault (the Needs attention / Worth a look lamps). Bright #6dff9c is kept for the mark and caret, the lamp in the current key, the GO key, the box being typed in, focus, 'mind', the status lamps that are on, her screens and the monitors.
decisions: Clean sheet (variants/r12-wild-4/sheet.css, 114 KB) under five system rules: one quote to a screen; everything else a key away; three type voices (Archivo condensed says what a thing is, Archivo what it says, IBM Plex Mono when, how many and where); three materials (green-black glass, plum-graphite solids, bone ink); phosphor is light, not paint.

The quote head is a system. page_head (in my _ui.html) takes figure, unit and now change: the figure sits in the section colour, with the unit stacked above a change line that begins with a small section-coloured arrow, on the figure's baseline. It runs on To do (4 OPEN / FIRST DUE SUN 27 SEP 19:56), the Plans month (3 AHEAD / NEXT TUE 29 SEP 17:00), the Plans list (the same), Ideas (12 IN ALL / LAST ADDED SUN 27 SEP) and Settings (1 TO LOOK AT). One way the data face writes a moment: a stamp macro in _ui.html turns a stored ISO value into SUN 27 SEP 19:56, working out the weekday with Sakamoto's rule so no view had to change. Give `.ask::before` at rest a plain `--edge` border and no 38px brand halo, lighting it only on `:focus-within` as it does now. Dim her older screens in the tape (`.said-bot:not(:last-child) .presence { opacity: .5; filter: saturate(.5) }`) so only the newest one glows. The card afterglow snaps off rather than fading: in motion-glow-1 the lilac edge is already gone, because the hover's radial-gradient background cannot transition and the 40% edge fades in about 300ms. Draw the hover light as box-shadow and border only and fade it over `var(--afterglow)`, as the kit's E9 does.

The command line reads dead on half the pages. `.caret { animation: blink 1.2s steps(1) 8 }` with `50% { opacity: 0 }` caught the cursor dark at shot time on Plans, Settings, General and the form. Blink it as phosphor does: `@keyframes blink { 50% { opacity: .3 } }`, keeping its halo. Make the words exact: `> SETTINGS > GENERAL▌`, `> IDEAS > NEW▌`, and `> ?NOT FOUND▌` on the 404 (it says READY today). On the phone `.cmd { display: none }` drops the terminal's voice where the family mostly uses it: under 48rem, show `.cmd` in place of `.brand-name` beside the mark. Slim the command row to about 2.5rem so the two sticky rows cost about 86px rather than 98px.

Numbers must mean one key each. The settings menu, the Settings index cells and the settings rail number their pages 1-9 with the same `kbd.key-n` chips as the function keys, so '1' is Home in the bar and General an inch below, and none of them has an access key. The Settings summary does have `accesskey="0"` but shows no 0. Put a `0` keycap on `.menu > summary`, and number its pages as sub-codes `0·1…0·9` in plain faint mono with no keycap (`.menu-list .key-n, .section-cards .key-n`). At the left end of `.keys`, add a quiet legend such as `ALT⇧` in violet mono, so 1-9 are not read as F-keys that do nothing.

Typesetting: prose is set in the data face, against the sheet's own rule 3. 'Times use America/Vancouver. A deadline…' runs to about 110 characters of IBM Plex Mono on To do. 'Google Calendar is not connected, so these are the plans the bot made.' is set in mono on Plans and wraps to three mono lines in the Home cell, and the save bar's 'An empty box uses the default it shows.' is mono too. Set `.source, .lede-data, .save-bar p` and the To do note in `400 var(--t-small)/1.5 var(--text)`, `--dim`, `max-width: 68ch`. Give the condensed display a little air: at 62% stretch 'What's on your mind?' and 'Things to do' crowd their spaces, so add `word-spacing: .05em` to `h1, .ask-question`. Use one date format in the data face: To do's `Due 2026-09-27 19:56` (the `row.due_input|replace` in tasks.html) against Home's 'Thursday 1 October, 10:00'. Pick one, such as `THU 01 OCT 10:00`.

Controls: make the field legends a rule, not a single form. Only `.idea-form label` and `.signin label` get violet mono caps; General's 'Home town or area', 'Time zone', 'Units' and To do's Add and Show fields are sans ink-2. Apply the legend style to `.form label:not(.check):not(.inline), .setting-head label`. The form's Kind combobox (`input[list]`) shows Chromium's grey ▼ and a faint 'restaurant' placeholder, so it looks disabled beside the live 'Suggested by' select. Hide `input[list]::-webkit-calendar-picker-indicator`, draw the same 1.5px chevron as `select::picker-icon`, and set its placeholder in `--dim`. The Settings summary's `icon('down')` is an arrow that reads as 'download', so use the chevron. Filter, Save a thought and Add something to do open over the list and cover To do's empty message: put `details[open] > .panel` in flow so it pushes the list down.

Status: red is the danger colour, but `.light.off { border: 2px solid var(--danger) }` spends it on seven lamps that are only switched off (no Gemini key, no Telegram token, weekend digest not sent), so the page reads alarmed and red competes with the green lamps. Draw off as an unlit lamp (`background: var(--led-off); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--line-2)`) and keep red for a real fault (`.lit-red`, a refused key). 'Today: about $0.00 of the $2.00 daily limit' repeats the readout beside it: replace it with the change figure (for example 'vs $0.14 yesterday') or drop it, and keep 'Change the limit'.

firstDraft.name: Single Quote
firstDraft.concept: FamilyDB as a trading terminal with a twist. Every screen quotes one thing large, as a quote screen shows a single security, and everything else sits a numbered key away. A thin command line (FamilyDB > IDEAS▌) and a function-key legend (1 Home … 6 Wishes, 7 Memory 8 Family 9 Status) frame each page. Below them the page's one thing is set in condensed display type with its figure beside it in the section's colour: her question on Home, the month on Plans, what today cost on Status, her newest line in the chat.
